consequences: Schema in docs/build-instructions.md §10 differs from the first draft (key, target_key, alias, line, frontmatter_error, meta). Image embeds never resolve to notes. Bump SCHEMA_VERSION in core/src/index.rs to rebuild.
context: Stage 1 index: links must resolve across NFC/NFD names, aliases and deletes, and the index must skip Brainstead's own writes.
decision: Compare by a key (NFC, lower case, base name without .md/.txt); resolve by file key then alias; target_id ON DELETE SET NULL; contentless FTS5 with contentless_delete; skip files whose size+mtime match, and only refresh the fingerprint when the sha256 matches.
title: Index keys and link resolution

consequences: Results and highlighting differ slightly from the previous app (stemming). Index SCHEMA_VERSION is 2. Details in docs/build-instructions.md §10 stage 2.
context: Porting the previous app's read view, lists and BM25 search to Brainstead's FTS5 index.
decision: Stemmed FTS5 search ranked by best passage with snippets; same query syntax; ghost links, heading/block links, backlinks for all layers by name or alias; sanitised raw HTML; syntax highlighting; every sources/ file indexed by name; unsupported task-query lines reported.
title: Stage 2 search and reading differ from the previous app

consequences: Both apps show the same captured items; nothing is written until the user turns read-only off; a refused shortcut is reported in Settings.
context: Stage 3 adds global quick capture while the previous app still runs on the same vault; Option-Space is often taken by Spotlight, Raycast or Alfred, and Command-Option-Space is Finder's search window.
decision: Default shortcut Control-Option-Space, changeable in Settings; tasks go under #### Other in Me. To Do List.md and thoughts to Me. Scratchpad.md, as the previous app writes them; read-only stays on by default; due:/defer: accept words and a picker.
title: Capture shortcut and destinations

consequences: No MDXEditor or normalisation layer; the fidelity test should pass by construction. Templates are trusted code, as in the previous app.
context: §5.1 planned MDXEditor first, but it re-serialises markdown it didn't change, against the never-reformat rule; Templater execution was open.
decision: Build the CodeMirror 6 live-preview editor from the start behind the Editor interface; run Templater blocks in the webview as a Function with a tp object.
title: Stage 4 editor and Templater

consequences: Accent and theme live in settings.json; colours are kept in step with the previous app by hand; the footer needs macOS (elsewhere the PDF has none).
context: The user asked for the previous app's professionally styled preview and PDF, following its print rules.
decision: Port the previous app's doc tokens, eight accents, per-app-overridable doc theme and print.css rules; title prints unless the body opens with an H1; Rust stamps a title and Page N of M footer with PDFKit because WebKit print has no page counters.
title: Documents and PDFs look as in the previous app

consequences: A note's own look is lost if it's renamed outside Brainstead; light or dark stays one choice for all documents.
context: The user asked for several contemporary document themes, a Settings › Notes section for the default theme and colour, keeping the override on the note screen, and the original Brainstead look as the default.
decision: Seven themes (Brainstead default, Business, Editorial, Modern, Minimal, Report, Technical) times eight colours; defaults in settings; the note screen overrides theme and colour for that note only, stored in settings by path (docLooks), never in the note.
title: Document themes with defaults in Settings and per-note overrides

consequences: No preview before creating a note (Test run in the template editor instead); null interpolations write nothing; numbered cursors put the caret at the lowest only.
context: Templates ran a subset of the previous app's with prompts collected by a dry run, which breaks templates whose questions depend on earlier answers; the user asked for full Templater support.
decision: Run templates as an async function top to bottom with questions asked live in the dialog; implement tp.date (moment, en-GB), tp.file, tp.frontmatter, tp.config, tp.hooks, tp.system (clipboard via Rust) and tp.user (scripts read by Rust from one vault folder); tp.obsidian, app and tp.web throw a clear 'not available in Brainstead' error.
title: Full Templater support with live prompts

consequences: No index schema change; the first query reads every markdown file once; TASK results aren't grouped by file or nested by subtask as Dataview shows them; no app API for scripts.
context: The user asked for full Dataview support; the SQLite index has no inline fields or list items, and another fork was changing the index schema for task queries.
decision: Rust parses each page's Dataview metadata on demand and keeps it by path, size and mtime, returning only pages changed since a generation the window passes back; DQL, the function library and DataviewJS run in the window (luxon for dates), with the same trust as templates; TASK results are the app's task rows, flat, with rank sorting enabling drag.
title: Dataview runs in the window over pages Rust parses and caches

consequences: One implementation for built-in and function clauses; every block fetches all tasks once per vault change (cached and shared); function clauses run with the vault owner's trust, as templates do.
context: The user asked for the Tasks plugin's full query language; it includes filter/sort/group by function, which are JavaScript.
decision: Parse and run the whole language in TypeScript (src/tasksq/) over every task Rust indexes (tasks_all), using moment, chrono-node and rrule like the plugin; Rust's own TaskQuery stays for the Tasks screen.
title: Task queries run in the window

consequences: Next occurrence goes on the line above; 'when done' counts from today; 🏁 delete removes the done line; ⌘Z restores the original line if the written lines are unchanged. Edit-mode ticks don't recur.
context: Ticking a recurring task must add its next occurrence, as the Tasks plugin does, in a vault also edited by other apps.
decision: The window computes the new lines (src/tasksq/edits.ts) and Rust replaces the one task line with them in a single atomic, mtime-keeping write (task_replace), recorded for undo as the original line and every line written.
title: Recurring task completion writes

consequences: Stage 5 ports review_window, week_inputs, session_logs, stuck_tasks, lint and upsert logic to Rust; no Bash for models; reviews no longer need the previous app's BFF.
context: The previous app's daily and weekly review skills write through vault Python scripts and read tasks from its BFF, all under --dangerously-skip-permissions; Brainstead forbids models writing to the vault.
decision: Brainstead gathers the review inputs in Rust (replacing the vault scripts), the model only composes the block with read-only tools, and the app upserts it into the monthly review file and appends log.md via the safe write, with Undo.
title: Scheduled reviews: the app writes the review block

consequences: Vault skills can be invoked with /name but anything beyond reading is refused; no agent files appear in the vault.
context: Claude Code should see the vault's CLAUDE.md and skills; Antigravity needs a custom agent file in its working folder to limit its tools, and nothing may be written into the vault by a model or for one.
decision: Claude, Codex and Copilot run with the vault as working directory; Antigravity runs in the app data folder ask/agy holding its read-only agent and gets the vault with --add-dir. Claude gets Read,Grep,Glob,Skill.
title: Ask runs in the vault; Antigravity in its own folder

consequences: Either app lists and resumes the other's chats; the previous app never tries to resume a Codex thread with Claude.
context: Both apps run alongside and the previous app saves chats as Chat. <title>.md in the vault; Brainstead's read-only mode refuses vault writes.
decision: Brainstead writes the same file format (plus sessionId for non-Claude CLIs and kind: review), keeps the previous app's 20-archived retention, and while read-only keeps chats in the app data chats/ folder until a save can reach the vault.
title: Chats saved in the previous app's format; local while read-only

consequences: Schema bump for task project/context/effort; new multi-line and two-file writes with undo.
context: Stage 6 makes projects, contexts, areas and effort first-class; the previous app had no project model and the vault must stay readable by other editors.
decision: Projects are Project. <name>.md notes with status, area and outcome properties; a task belongs by living in the note or linking [[Project]]. Contexts are #context/<name> tags; effort is [effort:: 15m]. The Inbox is Scratchpad blocks plus #### Other tasks, removed once clarified (with undo). The guided weekly review appends a Your review section to the week's block.
title: GTD formats: Project. notes, #context/ tags, effort field

consequences: No line moves are needed for most clarifies; the Inbox count is computed in the window (unclarified in src/Inbox.tsx).
context: Clarifying must take an item out of the Inbox, but an Other task clarified as a next action without a project would otherwise have nowhere to move to.
decision: An Other task is in the Inbox while it has no project, context, #waiting-for, #someday-maybe or #followup and isn't done; clarifying in place adds one of those. A next action must get a project or a context.
title: Inbox membership for To Do Other tasks

consequences: Fixtures and docs use the shared table consistently; new tests and examples must invent names too; the review workflows describe labelling generically; personal specifics live only on the user's machine.
context: The repo is going public; fixtures, docs, comments, UI text, sift records and the review workflows carried real names, the user's employer, private projects and data from the real vault.
decision: Use invented names only (Orbit App, Hub Platform, Maya, Lena, Sam Carter, Theo, Zara, Omar, Hugo, Victor; Acme, Northwind, Q4 Data, Ops, Role Framework; area Personal); call the replaced app 'the previous app' and the related apps 'the sibling apps'; real data never goes in the repo. Automated-session labels come from the user's local automated.json in the app data folder, not from the workflows.
title: Public repo: invented names only

consequences: No sqlite-vec dependency yet; quotes in PDFs are unchecked until 7b; the MCP server works with the app closed and from a terminal.
context: Stage 7 (knowledge engine) was too large for one checklist, and §9 left embeddings open.
decision: Split into 7a (MCP server, propose_edit, review queue, Knowledge health) and 7b (ingest, extraction, contradictions, jobs). No embeddings for now: FTS5, aliases, fuzzy. Citations are heading or PDF page anchors plus the quote in the proposal; sources are never edited. The MCP server is a stdio sidecar binary each CLI launches.
title: Stage 7 split; no embeddings; anchor+quote citations; stdio MCP

consequences: Antigravity chats can't propose edits; Settings › AI assistants says so.
context: Antigravity loads MCP servers from a workspace .agents/mcp_config.json and connects to Brainstead's, but its print mode (agy -p) refuses every MCP call regardless of permissions.allow (open CLI bug); the only workaround is --dangerously-skip-permissions.
decision: Ask gives the MCP server to Claude Code, Codex and Copilot only; Antigravity keeps its read-only agent tools. Revisit when agy's print mode honours allow rules.
title: Antigravity gets no MCP server in Ask

consequences: One signed program; CLI configs point at the app's executable path.
context: Stage 7a planned a bundled sidecar binary for the MCP server.
decision: The brainstead-mcp crate is a library the app's own binary runs when started with --mcp (and a small brainstead-mcp binary for terminals); no separate sidecar in the bundle.
title: MCP server runs as the app binary with --mcp

consequences: No background model calls on new sources; doc check, draft reply and bookmark triage move to a later stage.
context: Writing the stage 7b (ingest) checklist.
decision: Ingest only when the user starts it from Sources or a note's menu; the nightly job (contradictions on changed pages, index.md) has no cap; meeting note from a Teams transcript (single and batch) is in 7b; PDF text via macOS PDFKit behind platform, pure-Rust fallback elsewhere.
title: Stage 7b scope: manual ingest, uncapped nightly, meeting notes in, PDFKit

consequences: Captures work with the app closed and no port is opened; Chrome enforces the allowed IDs; the extensions need their own IDs in the host manifest, and the manifest install lives behind platform.
context: Stage 8 ports the Outlook and Teams capture extensions; the previous app used a localhost listener on a fixed port gated only by CORS.
decision: Use Chrome native messaging: a brainstead-capture binary in the bundle, on brainstead-core, writes captures through the safe write; the app installs the host manifest listing the allowed extension IDs.
title: Chrome extensions reach the app by native messaging

consequences: The review queue holds only what needs judgement; a wrong but quoted change lands in a page and is caught by Undo, log.md or a later contradiction check rather than before writing.
context: Accepting every ingest change in the review queue by hand was too tedious for the user; the rule was that no model writes to the vault without review.
decision: An ingest's change to an existing wiki page whose quotes are all found in the source is applied at once, with undo and a log.md line, unless Settings › AI assistants turns it off (autoApplyIngest, default on). New pages, name corrections, meeting notes, contradictions and unchecked quotes still go to the queue; the queue's Apply checked clears older ones.
title: Checked ingest changes are applied without review

consequences: §7 corrected; stage 8 isn't done until items 12-15 are; Help (item 7) still deferred.
context: The build doc's §7 said background jobs have a monthly budget while 7b said nightly jobs have no cap; the mock comparison (item 10) found three skill screens never built and gaps on Today, Tasks, source preview and wiki.
decision: No spending cap (usage bills through each CLI's account). Build Today/Tasks gaps, source provenance, wiki list/page gaps and the Triage bookmarks, Draft reply and Doc check screens as stage 8 items 12-15. Don't propose tasks/wiki edits when a note closes.
title: No AI spending cap; skill screens and polish gaps built in stage 8

consequences: Supersedes 'Ask is read-only' for memory only; other CLIs unchanged; tests guard the allow and deny rules.
context: A chat after a daily review couldn't save to memory: Claude Code ran with Read, Grep, Glob and Skill only. The user wants agents to remember and propose vault changes freely.
decision: Claude Code gets Edit and Write tools, allowed only for Claude Code's memory folder and denied the vault; vault changes stay proposals through the MCP tools, which every chat has.
title: Ask chats may write Claude Code's memory

consequences: Most auto-applied ingests are now additions; a change that rewrites a line waits in the review queue
context: The 2026-10-03 exception applied an ingest's change to an existing wiki page when its quotes were found, but failed claims were silently dropped, quotes could be a word or two, paths weren't confined to wiki/ and section replacement could delete the user's lines
decision: Auto-apply only when ingest::needs_review passes: existing page at wiki/<folder>/<name>.md, every claim's quote found (a missing one becomes a warning and the page is queued), every quote at least 20 characters, nothing removed from the page (body lines kept, properties unchanged but sources added and updated bumped), and with names corrected the quotes are in the on-disk text. Settings › AI assistants can still turn it off. Apply checked uses the same rule
title: Ingest auto-apply tightened

consequences: Slightly larger binary; a panic in one batch is logged and the batch skipped rather than crashing
context: panic=abort made any panic (one malformed file in the watcher) quit the app; catch_unwind is a no-op under abort
decision: profile.release panic = unwind; the watcher batch and vault open catch_unwind; mutexes are taken with crate::lock, which recovers poisoning; commands that touch the index run in spawn_blocking so a panic there becomes an error
title: Release builds unwind on panic

consequences: dataviewjs in wiki pages or sources no longer runs; any new Markdown call site is safe by default; tasksq parseQuery needs QueryFile.scripts true to compile functions
context: dataviewjs, inline $= and Tasks by-function code run with the app's full access (Tauri invoke, unsafe-eval), and Markdown drew captured email/Teams, Ask answers and model text
decision: Markdown's scripts prop defaults off; only Doc turns it on, for layer note outside sources/ and wiki/ (wiki is model-maintained and ingest can auto-apply). Elsewhere a quiet 'Scripts don't run in captured or AI content' replaces the script; DQL still renders
title: Scripts in rendered markdown run only in the user's own notes

consequences: A new table or list should use these classes rather than its own header/band/row styles; the scroller sets --tb-head to its header height so bands stick under it.
context: The user loved the Projects table (sticky header, shaded group bands with counts, divided rows, accent bar on the selected row) and asked for Tasks, Inbox, Activity, the review queue, Notes/Wiki/Sources and Trash to match.
decision: Shared CSS classes .tb-head, .tb-band (with .tb-group and a .n pill) and .tb-row in styles.css, and a TableBand component in src/ui.tsx; each screen keeps only its own grid columns and padding. Lists that are banded order their keyboard navigation by the displayed order.
title: Every list screen uses one table look

consequences: Today's bands are not sticky (position static inside the card). New Today sections should be a Band, not a separate card. Waiting-for age needs a created date (➕) on the task.
context: Today's three separate task cards, run-on summary sentence and tall two-line side cards were hard to take in at a glance; the user liked the shared table style (.tb-band/.tb-row).
decision: Count tiles under the greeting jump to bands; one card holds Overdue, Due today, Deferred until now and Waiting for as TableBand bands (empty ones hidden); right-rail cards use a band header and single-line divided rows; Draft nudge on Today is a hover/focus icon (DraftNudge compact), Projects keeps the full button.
title: Today is drawn as one banded table with count tiles

consequences: New line-edit helpers need no quote handling if they go through edit/inQuote. Undo restores whole lines, so edit_task must not re-prefix. The parity fixtures from the previous app don't list callout tasks, so none is in tests/fixtures/vault; the demo vault has one.
context: Tasks in callouts (> - [ ]) weren't listed because every line edit assumed the line starts with the list marker.
decision: Keep the whole line in line_text for finding it again; parsers read past the quote markers (tasks::split_quote, splitQuote); every edit applies to the inner line and puts the markers back (edits.rs edit, bulk_rank, inQuote, toggledLine). replace_task itself is unchanged: the window sends full lines.
title: Tasks inside quotes and callouts: the > markers are a container

consequences: A topic is added by dropping a file in src/help; no list to update. help.test.ts checks every screen and pane has a topic, links are valid app: links and the house rules hold. Changing a screen means updating its help file in the same change, as with docs/.
context: The user wanted in-app help, and Ask's agents able to answer questions about the app from it. An Apple Help Book was considered and rejected with the user.
decision: Topics are src/help/*.md (frontmatter plus ## sections). The window imports them raw (src/help/index.ts); Rust embeds them with core/build.rs (core/src/help.rs). Ask gets them through the MCP server's help tool, and Antigravity, which takes no MCP server, as files copied into help/ in its working folder. The keyboard shortcut sheet reads its list from src/help/keyboard.md.
title: Help is one set of markdown files shared by the drawer and Ask

consequences: Outside Claude Code sessions get the same tools through claude mcp add brainstead. Stage 9 (everything through MCP) is drafted in the build doc and waits on which changes may skip the queue.
context: Ask told the user it couldn't write a note: propose_edit only made new wiki pages. The user wants Ask and outside sessions to author and edit notes.
decision: create_note proposes a new note outside sources/, wiki/ and Templates/, in an existing folder, named by Brainstead from type, title and date (filename::compose); existing names are refused. Edits to existing notes stay with propose_edit. Everything still waits in the review queue.
title: New notes through MCP: create_note, named by the app, via the review queue

consequences: One copy of each behaviour. A new screen action should get an action in mcpActions.ts and a tool in mcp/src/lib.rs, and a name in ask::MCP_TOOLS (a test checks). Actions need the app; reads don't.
context: The user wants everything in Brainstead possible through the MCP server, for Ask and outside sessions. Some behaviour exists only in the window (recurrence, priority edits, Templater) and runs need the app.
decision: Reads stay in the MCP process. Actions are request files in the app data folder's bridge/ that the running app hands to the window, which runs the screens' own functions (src/mcpActions.ts). The server opens the app when it isn't running. Task edits, Inbox clarify, projects, bookmarks, safe fixes and runs happen at once with a toast and undo; prose, renames and deletes are proposals; assistants may accept or reject proposals.
title: Everything through MCP: actions run in the app's window via a file bridge

consequences: Non-macOS builds offer no voices, so the button and settings hide. New markup that shouldn't be read goes in blocks.ts's SKIP list.
context: The user wanted notes and wiki pages read aloud with a voice setting, a player bar and a hotkey, built on the approach a sibling app already proved.
decision: Native AVSpeechSynthesizer from Rust (platform/speech.rs) with synchronous commands, not WebKit speechSynthesis; one block per utterance; spoken text and highlight map from one DOM walk; generation ids guard every event; Now Playing for media keys; caffeinate while playing. Hotkey Shift-Cmd-P (Note > Read Aloud); Space, F8, F7/F9 and Esc while reading. Reading stops on leaving the note or switching to Edit/Source; query blocks are summarised; code, maths and citations skipped; English voices; word highlight by default; no sleep timer; clicking a paragraph reads from there; the player bar is draggable.
title: Read aloud through AVSpeechSynthesizer, a block at a time, with generation-tagged utterances

consequences: Keep the asset name Brainstead.dmg. Each release: make app, make dmg, commit, push, gh release create.
context: Brainstead was install-from-source only; the sibling apps ship an unnotarised DMG on GitHub releases.
decision: Publish Brainstead.dmg (Apple silicon, macOS 14+) on GitHub releases like the siblings; the first release is 1.0.0, and make app bumps the patch from there. The README's Download section links to releases/latest/download/Brainstead.dmg.
title: Release as a DMG on GitHub releases, starting at 1.0.0

consequences: Glance.tsx holds the pies; the data comes from the glance command (core activity.rs). A sixth colour would need validating, not inventing; fold more into Other instead.
context: The user wanted notes and wiki pages by type, top tags and a word cloud, and preferred pie charts to bars.
decision: Activity gets Notes by type and Notes by tag pies plus a Most linked list (inbound links from distinct files); Knowledge health gets Wiki pages by type and by tag pies as its first side card. No word cloud. Each pie shows the top five then Other, with a legend naming every slice; slices and rows open the filtered list. Colours are new tokens --pie-1..5 and --pie-other, validated for colour blindness in both themes.
title: Vault at a glance: pie charts on Activity and Knowledge health

consequences: One extra assistant call per answer; the hint appears a few seconds after the answer. Reviews and failed turns get none.
context: Wanted high-quality next-turn suggestions in Ask, accepted with the right arrow. Options: the answering model appends a hidden line (free, lower quality) or a second call after each answer.
decision: A second call (ask_next) after each answer, with its own job model (suggest, default as new chats) and an on/off switch (askSuggest, default on) in Settings › AI assistants. It sees the chat title and the last three exchanges, may read the vault but changes nothing. Shown as the empty box's placeholder; → or Tab types it. Dropped if the chat moved on meanwhile; never saved.
title: Ask suggests the next message with a separate model call

consequences: Accepted new notes carry one extra property. A script the user asked an assistant to write needs the property removed before it runs.
context: D-20261003-05 keeps scripts to the user's own notes, but notes an assistant created (create_note, meeting notes, Ask Save as note, contradiction and doc-check reports) and saved chats landed outside wiki/ and sources/, so their dataviewjs, $= and by-function code ran.
decision: proposals::make adds created-by: assistant to every new non-wiki note; the window adds it to the notes it saves from model text. scriptsAllowed also refuses type: chat and Me. Daily/Weekly Reviews files. Accepted edits to the user's own notes are not marked: the user saw the diff. Deleting the property trusts a note.
title: Notes an assistant writes are marked created-by: assistant; their scripts don't run

consequences: New top-bar actions go before the view switch; Ask stays rightmost.
context: The note, wiki, source and template pages placed Ask and their own actions in different orders.
decision: One order on every document page: Save (when dirty), the page type's actions (Refresh from sources; Draft a reply or Doc check; Test run then Templater docs), View/Edit/Source, bookmark, copy, rename, graph, read aloud, text size, more, then Ask beside the help button. Any screen with an Ask button puts it last.
title: Ask is the last button in a top bar, beside help

consequences: A new screen gets Ask by passing ask to TopBar; no hand-made Ask buttons in top bars.
context: Ask buttons sat in different places and only asked about the screen in general.
decision: TopBar takes ask={about, prompt} and draws Ask last, beside help. about finishes the tooltip 'Ask about …' and names the selection when there is one (task, project, Inbox item, proposal, clash, graph page, document), else the screen; prompt is typed into a new chat to finish. Left off the AI flows (Meeting, Triage, Draft reply, Doc check) and the Trash.
title: Every screen's Ask button is context sensitive and drawn by TopBar

consequences: A tp function added to the engine needs adding to TP in templaterAssist.ts.
context: Writing templates meant looking up tp functions in Templater's docs.
decision: src/editor/templaterAssist.ts offers, inside a <% tag in a template, only the tp functions the engine runs (a test runs each through runTemplate), plus tp.user scripts; each inserts as a CodeMirror snippet with its arguments as fields and adds %> if the tag is open. tp.web, tp.obsidian and tp.app aren't offered.
title: Templater help: tp completions after <% in templates

consequences: @codemirror/lang-javascript is a direct dependency. A tp function added to the engine still needs adding to TP.
context: Tags were tinted as whole blocks, and completion only knew tp functions, not const, await or the template's own names.
decision: templaterSyntax colours the code inside tags with the JavaScript parser and classHighlighter (tok-* classes in the code blocks' colours) in Edit and Source, and templaterHtml draws the same in View. templaterAssist completes inside a tag from a JavaScript state of every earlier tag's code plus the current one, as the engine compiles them into one function: keywords, locals, tp/tR/moment, JS globals and their members, and tp modules then functions. Supersedes D-20261004-06's tp-only list.
title: Templater scripts: coloured as JavaScript in every mode, completed as JavaScript

consequences: A topic that covers a document type should set page:.
context: Help for a template, wiki page or source opened its list's topic on the first section, so what mattered on the page sat folded.
decision: A topic's frontmatter page: names the section to open first when the topic is shown for an open document of its kind (templates: Write a template, wiki: Read a wiki page, sources: Preview a source); otherwise the first section opens. A test checks each page: names a real section.
title: Help on an open document opens the section for its page type

consequences: Errors can't be missed; a burst of errors stacks until dismissed.
context: The UI audit (2026-10-04) found error toasts vanished after 2.6 s like success ones, before messages like 'changed since read' could be read.
decision: Toasts with tone bad stay until the user closes them, have a close button and use role=alert; other toasts still time out.
title: Error toasts stay until closed

consequences: A task lives in one GTD list at a time; New task feels local to the list.
context: Audit 2026-10-04: To Do › Other items showed in both the Inbox and Next actions, and New task always went to the Inbox whatever list was open.
decision: Next actions leaves out tasks the Inbox counts as unclarified (same rule). New task on a list gets that list's context, tag or project so it appears there; lists with none still send it to the Inbox.
title: Unclarified Inbox tasks stay out of Next actions; New task takes the list's context

consequences: New UI text uses these words; help and the Shortcuts sheet match.
context: Audit 2026-10-04 found the same idea named differently across screens (Scheduled/Deferred/Defer until; Clarify all with AI/Suggest for each; Promote/Ingest; Delete/Move to the Trash).
decision: Use Deferred everywhere (Starts stays, explained); Suggest / Suggest for all for AI suggestions; Ingest into the wiki; Move to the Trash.
title: One name per thing: Deferred, Suggest, Ingest into the wiki, Move to the Trash

consequences: Help, docs and CLAUDE.md say verified.
context: 'Apply checked' read as ticked items in a list with no checkboxes.
decision: The button is Apply verified changes, qualifying rows carry a Quotes verified chip, and the setting reads Apply verified ingest changes straight away. The stored setting key is unchanged.
title: Verified, not checked, for ingest changes applied at once

consequences: Turning read-only off stays a deliberate act in Settings.
context: Read-only is on by default for an existing vault and nothing in the shell said so.
decision: A Read-only pill in the sidebar status line and tray header; clicking it opens Settings › Vault.
title: Read-only pill opens Settings › Vault, it doesn't toggle

consequences: General starts with real settings; Jobs is about scheduled jobs only.
context: Settings › General opened on a migration checklist for everyone; ingest switches were split between AI assistants and Jobs.
decision: The checklist shows only when the previous app's files are in the vault. All ingest switches form one Ingest group in AI assistants below the model choice. The Jobs master switch stays, since it stops two apps running the reviews.
title: Settings layout: the Moving over checklist only when the previous app is found; ingest switches grouped

consequences: Help and docs use the two names consistently.
context: 'Weekly review' named both the interactive screen and the scheduled AI job, and the screen had no sidebar entry.
decision: UI text calls the job weekly summary (storage keys unchanged); the Weekly review screen gets a sidebar entry.
title: Weekly summary is the job; Weekly review is the screen

consequences: Each problem is shown once.
context: The 'New in Brainstead' group name only made sense to users of the previous app, and Ghost links and stale-page cards repeated the list.
decision: Rename the group More checks and drop the duplicate side cards.
title: Knowledge health: More checks, no duplicate side cards

consequences: The mode is obvious at a glance.
context: Edit and Source looked almost the same.
decision: Source shows raw markdown in monospace with no styling and no formatting toolbar; Edit is unchanged.
title: Source mode is plain monospace

consequences: Starter notes ship in the app and use invented names only.
context: Welcome assumed an existing vault and said nothing about the app.
decision: Welcome says what Brainstead is and offers Create a new vault, which makes a folder filled with example notes showing the key features, each saying it's an example you can delete, plus a Start here note. A vault the app creates opens read-write; existing vaults still open read-only.
title: First run can create a new vault with example notes

consequences: Text like 'costs $5 and $10' stays as it is.
context: The fixture had inline maths that stayed raw; vault notes also contain money like $5.
decision: Render $…$ and $$…$$ with KaTeX, bundled locally, using pandoc's rule: the opening $ is followed by a non-space; the closing $ is preceded by a non-space and not followed by a digit; \$ escapes.
title: Inline maths renders, money does not

consequences: OCR runs once per image in the background; CLAUDE.md's auto-apply rule notes the image exception.
context: Health offered Ingest for images that Sources refused; the user wants image ingestion throughout.
decision: Images (png, jpg, heic, webp, gif; not svg) are OCR'd with macOS Vision for search and quotes. Assistants that can see images (Claude Code, Codex) get the picture too. Changes from an image always go to the review queue, never auto-applied. With no text and an assistant that can't see images, ingest refuses.
title: Images are ingestible sources; their changes are always queued

consequences: No core change to keep rejected proposals.
context: Reject all threw away every proposal in one click.
decision: Reject all asks for confirmation; single Reject and Reject all have no undo.
title: Reject all asks first; no undo for rejects

consequences: An existing vault is never opened writable by accident.
context: Read-only was one global setting, so switching to another existing folder kept whatever it was; new vaults made by the app should open read-write.
decision: A vault Brainstead creates opens with Read-only off; picking a different existing folder sets Read-only on; picking the same folder leaves it.
title: Choosing a different vault folder turns Read-only back on

consequences: Starter notes are in the public repo, so invented names only.
context: Create a new vault needs example notes.
decision: The examples live in src-tauri/starter-vault/, embedded by core/build.rs; dates are filled in on write; Settings › Vault › Add the example notes adds only missing files.
title: Starter vault embedded in the app

consequences: New users don't see a migration checklist.
context: The Moving over checklist should show only for people coming from the previous app.
decision: It shows when the vault has scripts/substitutions.json or one of the previous app's scripts (lint_wiki.py, upsert_review_block.py, log_append.py, review_window.py, session_logs.py); .claude/skills alone doesn't count. Jobs got its own Show the file button for automated.json.
title: Previous app detected by its scripts/ files

consequences: Same key for the same action on both screens.
context: Triage's Promote to wiki became Ingest into the wiki.
decision: Its key changed from P to I, matching the Inbox.
title: Triage ingest key is I

consequences: New images become searchable a few at a time; showing images to the model is macOS-only for now.
context: Vision's first OCR in a session can take a minute; Copilot and Antigravity CLIs take no image input.
decision: Images are OCR'd in the background after open (text kept by content hash). Claude Code (--add-dir) and Codex (--image) get a ≤2000px JPEG; Copilot and Antigravity get OCR text only and refuse an image with no text. SVG isn't ingestible.
title: Image OCR runs after the vault opens; only Claude Code and Codex see images

consequences: Startup stays light; print before KaTeX loads shows raw text.
context: Rendering $…$ must not catch money.
decision: A micromark construct in src/md/math.ts applies pandoc's rule; KaTeX and its fonts load on the first note with maths; a formula it can't read shows as raw text.
title: Maths: pandoc dollar rule, KaTeX loaded lazily

consequences: Old files, trash and undo records keep working. target::old_name/new_name is the one mapping; the frozen script fixtures stay on the old names and are compared through fixture::renamed.
context: The scheduled jobs became the daily and weekly summary in the UI; the vault kept Me. Daily/Weekly Reviews files and ## Daily/Weekly review headings.
decision: New runs write Me. Daily Summaries - YYYY-MM.md / Me. Weekly Summaries - YYYY-MM.md, ## Daily summary YYYY-MM-DD / ## Weekly summary YYYY-Www, and log.md details daily-summary / weekly-summary. Every reader (weekly gather, stuck check, previous block, Weekly screen, session detection, origin labels, Recent runs, scripts guard) accepts the old names too; a re-run or Finish updates the block where it is (Window::locate), even in an old file.
title: Summary files and headings renamed; readers accept the old names

consequences: Settings labels, run names and proposal labels changed; storage names follow in D-20261004-28.
context: The user wanted both scheduled jobs named as summaries, leaving 'review' for the GTD weekly review.
decision: UI, help and docs call them the daily summary and weekly summary (together, the daily and weekly summaries); 'Weekly review' is only the guided GTD screen.
title: Daily summary, not daily review

consequences: review_latest command and api.reviewLatest; block_of moved from the app's weekly.rs to core reviews::latest.
context: The user wanted the summaries readable on Today; the Daily summary row in To process only linked to the note.
decision: Two cards in Today's right rail, folded by default (state in viewMemory, today.dailySummary / today.weeklySummary). Daily: latest block within 31 days. Weekly: on weeklyDay and the day after, this week's or last week's block. Shown when reviewsHere or a block exists. The To process row is gone; its status line moved to the card header. Core: reviews::latest via Window::locate, so old names are read.
title: Today shows the daily and weekly summaries as folding cards

consequences: The lists match what was written this week; edits to older notes don't appear.
context: Process this week's notes and Look back listed every note modified this week, so old notes that were only edited crowded the lists.
decision: Both steps list only notes whose name carries a full date (… - YYYY-MM-DD) inside the week. Notes without a day in the name aren't listed. The weekly summary's gathering is unchanged.
title: Weekly review lists notes dated in the week

consequences: Older transcripts whose name date is their capture day now ask for a date check. The extension's manifest is 1.1.0; users reload it in chrome://extensions after opening Settings › Capture extensions. Extension tests run under Vitest (extensions/**/*.test.js).
context: A transcript captured with the Teams extension was named with the capture day, and the meeting note screen dated the note from the file name, so captures after midnight or days later got the wrong date.
decision: The extension reads the meeting's date and start from the recap page (extensions/teams-capture/meeting-date.js, several places and English formats, nothing rather than a guess) and sends meetingDate/meetingStart. webcapture.rs names a transcript with meetingDate when valid and writes '**Meeting:** <date> <start>' above '**Captured:**'; without it, unchanged. meeting.rs takes the date from '**Meeting:**' over the name; when the name's date equals the '**Captured:**' local day and there's no Meeting line, it sets dateCheck, and the Meeting screen (and the MCP meeting_note action) won't draft until the date is confirmed or changed.
title: Teams transcripts are dated with the meeting's day

consequences: An older dated note edited later no longer appears in the later day's summary.
context: Meeting notes written up after midnight showed in the wrong day's summary, and a past day's summary couldn't be rewritten.
decision: The daily and weekly summaries gather a journal note by its own full date (name or date property) when it has one, else by the day it changed. Run now, and start_run's date, write the summary for a chosen past day or that day's week.
title: Summaries count a dated note on its own date; Run now can take a day

consequences: Batch write-ups after midnight don't appear as the next day's work.
context: Meeting notes written up after midnight showed in the next day's summary through log.md's ingest entries.
decision: Log entries naming a note with a day in its name count only in that day's window, and entries naming a note that has since been renamed or deleted are left out.
title: A day's summary leaves out log entries about notes dated another day

consequences: Moving the weekly summary no longer moves the review reminder. Settings saved before have the default. Changing it doesn't re-stamp any job's schedule.
context: Today reminded you of the guided weekly review on the weekly summary's day, tying when you review to when the AI summary runs.
decision: The Weekly review gets its own day and time (reviews.weeklyReviewDay / weeklyReviewTime in settings, default Friday 16:00), set in Settings › Jobs & schedule with no switch or Run now. Today shows the reminder from that time on that day and all the next day, and always while a review is paused.
title: Weekly review has its own day and time

consequences: Finish writes into the reviewed week's block even if done after the week ends. A paused review left for over a week is dropped for a fresh one.
context: The Weekly review screen covered the ISO week of today, so a review done on a Monday or Tuesday covered a week that had barely started, unlike the weekly summary.
decision: A new review covers the week weekly_target picks (on a Monday or Tuesday last week, otherwise this week; reviewWeek in src/Weekly.tsx). A paused review keeps its own week until the next week's review is due (keepsPaused: its week is no older than reviewWeek of a week ago).
title: Weekly review covers the week by the summary's rule; a paused review keeps its week

consequences: Nothing is written by the job: the window applies an accepted suggestion through the app's own undoable actions, and a link becomes a review-queue proposal (weekprep_link). Settings' Models by job list needs a weekprep row (UI piece).
context: The user wanted AI suggestions for every step of the guided weekly review, ready before sitting down to it, and never applied without a click.
decision: A background job (src-tauri/src/weekprep.rs) runs on the weekly review day prep::LEAD_HOURS (4, a constant) before weeklyReviewTime, at midnight if that would fall the day before, only while reviewsHere is on, and only if the week has no preparation or the vault stamp (prep::stamp: the week's notes, every open task's line, the Inbox, stuck projects, notes dated ahead; not the day) has changed. It also runs on weekprep_ensure (review started; same check) and weekprep_run (always). One model call with read-only tools via the assistant CLI, as the summaries run, shown as a tab in Ask; model from Models by job key weekprep, defaulting to the summaries' (reviews) model. Saved per week in weekly-prep/<week>.json with preparedAt, model and stamp; 12 weeks kept. Moving the review's day or time, or taking the jobs on, stamps the schedule so it first fires at its next time.
title: Weekly review preparation job

consequences: Suggestions carry the task's path, line and lineText so the window finds it with findTask; ids hash step, action and words, so a re-prepared week keeps the same ids for the same suggestions.
context: A model preparing the weekly review can misquote notes, invent tasks, repeat existing ones or refer to tasks it wasn't given.
decision: prep::parse keeps a suggestion only if its step is one of the ten (loose, inbox, notes, back, next, ahead, projects, waiting, someday, creative); its action, if any, is one of add, tick, defer, waiting, someday, edit, clarify, link with refs (T1, I1) to tasks and Inbox items it was given; its source quote is found in the note by proposals::normalise_quote, the ingest check, also reading links as their shown words; a new task's words (task_words, the rule of taskWords in src/mcpActions.ts) aren't already a task; a defer is after today; a link's target is an existing page the note doesn't link yet. Dropped ones are counted and logged.
title: Prepared suggestions are checked like ingest quotes

consequences: No new write paths beyond task_add. A suggestion whose task or Inbox item changed since preparation fails with a message rather than acting on the wrong line.
context: The weekly review preparation saves suggestions per week; the Weekly review screen needs to show and act on them without a model writing to the vault.
decision: Each step shows its suggestions as rows with one action and Skip. Accepting uses the app's own undoable actions: taskModel/tasksq edits for tasks, mcpActions' clarifyItem for Inbox items, a new undoable task_add (Quick capture's placement under To Do > Other) or project_add_task for new tasks, and weekprep_link for links via the review queue. Accepted and skipped ids are kept in WeeklyState.handled so they stay hidden after a pause; accepted ones go in the review log. The creative step's prompts show on New ideas, loose and creative are prompts only. The Inbox shows the prepared clarify suggestions as its own.
title: Weekly review suggestions: accepted through existing undoable actions, remembered in the review's progress

consequences: Models by job lists weekprep, showing the summaries' model as its fallback. The eval scenario 'prepare the weekly review' runs prep::gather/prompt/parse on the fixture vault.
context: The preparation job had no off switch, no Stop and no place in Settings › Jobs & schedule.
decision: Setting weekprepEnabled (ui map, default on) gates the schedule only; Run now and opening the review still prepare. weekprep_job gives last run and next time (null when off or reviewsHere is off); weekprep_stop cancels the run. Switching it back on stamps the schedule, like taking the jobs over. Its runs stay out of Recent runs, which is typed to the summaries (Show/Undo); the row has Open for the last run's chat. MCP start_run/run_status/stop_run take weekly_prep.
title: Weekly review preparation: its own switch and job row

consequences: Suggestions stay stable through a review; a review started long after the noon run may show older suggestions until Prepare again.
context: weekprep_ensure re-ran the preparation whenever the vault changed, and working through the review changes it, so returning to the screen started over.
decision: Opening the review prepares only when the week has no preparation; the scheduled run still refreshes a stale one; Prepare again is the manual refresh.
title: Opening the weekly review doesn't prepare it again

consequences: New vaults, and Settings › Vault › Add the example notes (missing files only), get the templates. Start here lists them; help (templates, settings-vault) and docs/notes.md mention them. A starter template that stops running fails vitest.
context: Brainstead runs Templater templates, but a new vault had only one example (Meeting), so nothing showed what the engine can do. The release was to ship example templates.
decision: src-tauri/starter-vault/Templates/ holds Meeting, Daily note, 1-1, Project, Weekly plan and Reading note, plus Snippets/End of day.md (included by Daily note) and scripts/quarter.js (tp.user.quarter, called by Weekly plan). Each opens with a Templater comment saying it's an example, what it shows, and that it can be deleted. Project uses tp.file.rename to Project. <name> at the vault root (there is no projects folder); Reading note shows tp.file.move into Reading/. src/notes/starterTemplates.test.ts runs every starter template in the engine with answered prompts. The meeting-note scaffold now also fills variables chosen with tp.system.suggester, since the 1-1 template picks the person that way, and the vault's unresolved-link count leaves out templates, whose [[<% … %>]] links are only made when they run. The starter vault is exempt from the licence header check: its files become the user's.
title: Example templates ship in the starter vault

consequences: A feature isn't done until assistants can use it; reviews check lib.rs and mcpActions.ts alongside the help.
context: Several features added on 2026-10-04 (summaries, weekly review preparation, deferred naming) reached the screens before the MCP tools, so assistants lagged behind the app.
decision: Every new feature and every change to an existing one updates the MCP server in the same change: a read tool, and a change tool where the screen changes something, using the UI's names. Written into CLAUDE.md's rules.
title: Every feature is supported by the MCP server

consequences: Old names keep working for assistants with cached schemas. A suggestion accepted by an assistant is hidden on screen and logged like a click.
context: The scheduled jobs became the daily and weekly summaries, the guided GTD screen is the Weekly review, and the scheduled task view is shown as Deferred; the MCP tools still used the old names.
decision: start_run, run_status and stop_run list daily_summary and weekly_summary and still accept daily_review and weekly_review unlisted; list_tasks lists deferred and accepts scheduled (the view id stays scheduled so saved lists keep working). New tools: summary (read in Rust, no app needed), weekly_review (read, through the app) and weekly_suggestion (accept or skip a prepared suggestion through the screen's own choice() actions, recorded in the saved weekly state; an open Weekly review reloads on a window event).
title: MCP: summaries and Deferred named as the app names them; weekly review tools

consequences: System notes can only be removed outside the app.
context: Only five notes found by name were protected; summaries notes, index.md, log.md and notes marked with the system-note callout could be deleted.
decision: rename::is_system (named notes, CLAUDE.md/index.md/log.md, the summaries notes) and says_system (the opening 'This is a system note' callout) guard trash and rename in the core, so screens and MCP tools both refuse; the file menu greys the items. Undoing a summary run that created its note uses trash::undo_created.
title: System notes can't be trashed or renamed

consequences: Old reviews stay as ### Your review sections in summary blocks until migrated by hand. reviews::note holds the name and the compose rule; weekly.rs with_section is gone. The weekly summary prompt says Me. Weekly Review - … is the user's review, not a summary.
context: Finish and save on the guided Weekly review added a ### Your review section to the week's block in the monthly weekly summaries note, the AI job's output; the user wants their reviews kept apart from the summaries.
decision: Finish writes one note per week, Me. Weekly Review - YYYY-Www.md in the vault root (not Me. Weekly Reviews - …, the summaries' old name): title, the week's dates and finish time, steps done, the step log with accepted suggestions, and the user's notes. Finishing the same week again rewrites everything above its ## Added later heading and keeps that heading and what follows; if the heading is gone the whole old note is kept under a new one. Atomic write refusing a changed file, a weekly-review entry in log.md, undoable with Cmd-Z (note and log). Not a system note. The weekly summary gathers the note as an input; the summaries' upsert still carries over an existing ### Your review section (old data), and Finish no longer writes one. The Weekly review side pane links the note once it exists; MCP weekly_review reports its path (weekly_review_note command).
title: Weekly reviews have their own notes

consequences: No flashing and about 70s for the 44 docs images. The window chrome is drawn, not captured: if macOS changes its buttons, chrome() in the script needs new measurements. Screenshots are macOS only (platform::snapshot).
context: Retaking the docs screenshots flashed app windows on screen, which the user found hard on the eyes, and running several at once gave blank captures of covered windows. An invisible window's own capture is blank too.
decision: In screenshot mode the window is fully transparent, click-through, out of the Dock and never takes focus. The app saves WKWebView's takeSnapshot to BRAINSTEAD_SNAPSHOT after BRAINSTEAD_SNAPSHOT_AFTER seconds; tools/screenshots.py draws the unfocused window buttons and rounded corners back on, retries a blank shot from a fresh launch, and runs 4 apps at once (-j) with --docs for the docs scenes only. window_id.swift is gone; Screen Recording permission and swiftc are no longer needed.
title: Screenshots are taken unseen, from the webview's snapshot

consequences: No text recognition during screenshots; a scene that needed an image's text would have to rely on text kept in the demo's app data.
context: During screenshot runs, with several app copies starting at once, the macOS ANECompilerService (which prepares on-device models for Vision's text recognition) got stuck at 100% CPU and ignored a plain kill. The shots don't need image text.
decision: vault::text_cache gives no image reader when BRAINSTEAD_SCENE is set: images already read keep their kept text, others stay unread and aren't cached as unread. The normal app is unchanged.
title: Screenshot mode doesn't read the text in images

consequences: Inline styles are allowed in release as the CSP always said; scripts keep Tauri's nonces. Screenshot mode also turns off WKWebView's window-occlusion detection, or the invisible window gets no animation frames and CodeMirror never places popups.
context: In the installed app the template editor's popups were broken (tooltips far above the word, an unbounded bulleted completion list, a blue focus ring). The dev build was fine. Tauri adds a nonce to style-src in release builds, and a nonce makes browsers ignore 'unsafe-inline', so CodeMirror's runtime <style> element (and any other library's) was blocked.
decision: tauri.conf.json sets dangerousDisableAssetCspModification: ["style-src"], so the CSP's 'unsafe-inline' for styles applies as written. tools/screenshots.py --release runs the built app to check things only a release shows; scenes can put the caret or the mouse in the editor (caret, hover).
title: Tauri leaves style-src alone, so inline styles work in release builds

consequences: weekly:begun lives on the history entry only (useViewState with remember false), so each visit from the sidebar starts on the start page. The weekly scene sets it; weekly-start shows the page.
context: Opening Weekly review from the sidebar dropped you on step 1 and started the AI preparation, with no word on when the review is scheduled.
decision: The sidebar opens a start page: the week, the schedule (with Change), how the suggestions stand, and Start the review, or Carry on and Start over for a paused review. Opening it prepares nothing; Start does, as before. Today's Start or Carry on and the command palette go straight into the review.
title: Weekly review opens on a start page; only Start prepares it

consequences: Existing Chat notes in the vault count as saved. While the vault is read-only, a saved chat's turns go to app data and the note is left alone (and never deleted from there). A run's chat can be gone from Recent runs once 20 newer unsaved chats exist.
context: Every chat and every background run's chat was written to the vault after each turn, and unpinned vault chats beyond 20 were trashed. The user wants chats in the vault only when they choose; Weekly review sat under Today in the sidebar.
decision: A chat lives in the app data folder (chats/) until Ask's Save (chat_save keep, or the MCP tool save_chat) puts it in the vault; after that its turns keep the note up to date. Background runs' chats stay local too. Unsaved, unpinned closed chats beyond the latest 20 are deleted (open tabs never); saved chats are never cleared. Sidebar: Today, Inbox, Tasks, Projects, Weekly review, Review queue, Ask.
title: Ask chats stay out of the vault until saved; sidebar in GTD order

consequences: The review queue becomes Changes (a feed with Revert, held changes on top). The stale machinery, Apply verified changes and autoApplyIngest go; propose_edit becomes edit_page. CLAUDE.md's review-queue rule changes when it's built.
context: The review queue asked the user to approve almost every agent change (103 of 124 accepted) and proposals to one page went stale once one was accepted. The vault has one user and agents working for them.
decision: Changes the user started (Ask, a terminal session, a run started by hand) apply at once, flagged if a quote check fails. Scheduled changes apply at once when they pass every check; held when a check fails, they rewrite or remove the user's own notes' text, clash with unsaved edits, or contradict another page. Renames and trash apply at once. Held changes keep the agent's instruction and run on the page as it is. Every agent change is recorded for Revert, 90 days or 500 MB. The plan is plans/agent-changes.md.
title: Agent changes: act first, review by exception (supersedes AI proposes, you decide)

consequences: The always-held rule is stricter than the plan, which only flagged checks on user-started changes. MCP change tools need the app open (they go through change.submit). The old queue is migrated once on startup; proposals-backup/ and the legacy Proposal type in core/src/proposals.rs go after one release.
context: Building plans/agent-changes.md. Applying assistants' changes at once means an assistant's text, which may carry what a captured source told it, can reach notes where scripts run with the app's full access. Changes needed a run to group by, and on-arrival ingests and Health fixes needed a trigger.
decision: A change to Templates/ or one that adds runnable code (dataviewjs, inline $=, Tasks 'by function', Templater <% %>) is held for the user whoever started it (changes::needs_the_user). Held changes keep an Instruction; changes made from whole texts become find-and-replace edits with enough context to be found once (changes::from_texts). Origin gains run (the group: an ingest, nightly-<time> for the nightly check and everything it starts, a summary's run, the chat or the terminal session) and trigger (scheduled, or none for the user). Ingests of captures as they arrive, files dropped into Sources, Knowledge health fixes, weekly-review links, File this answer and Triage count as started by the user. The nightly catalogue for index.md is applied, not proposed. A summary's own Undo marks its change reverted. Edit before accepting marks a held change applied with no Revert (the editor's save is the write).
title: Changes: what's held whoever started it, and how runs are grouped

consequences: Rename MCP tools outright until the server is released; old Ask sessions just see the new names.
context: The agent-changes plan kept propose_edit as an alias for edit_page for one release.
decision: The MCP server isn't released, so renamed tools get no aliases: propose_edit is gone, only edit_page and changes exist.
title: No MCP aliases for renamed tools

consequences: Trash entries can now be folders (layer 'folder'). Ask's / picker loses the vault skills and lists Brainstead's own.
context: The vault's .claude/skills and scripts/ from the previous app had agents in a terminal write files directly, past Changes. The user has stopped using the previous app.
decision: Settings › General › Moving over gets a step, offered once 'The other app is stopped' is ticked: .claude/skills/ and scripts/ go to Brainstead's Trash as folders (restorable), name corrections are copied out first, and CLAUDE.md gets a marked brainstead block (after its first heading) telling agents to change the vault only through the MCP tools; undoable with ⌘Z. The checklist keeps showing once CLAUDE.md has the block. app_status tells an agent when the old skills are still there; retiring is done from the screen only.
title: Retiring the previous app's skills and scripts

consequences: Not scheduled, so no surprise model use. An MCP tool lists, accepts and skips the suggestions.
context: The user wants Brainstead to scan the vault and recommend projects and tasks. The weekly review's preparation already suggests tasks from a week's notes, each backed by a quote checked against its note.
decision: An on-demand run (button, ⌘K, MCP start_run) reads the user's notes changed or dated in the last 90 days, not the wiki or sources, and suggests tasks and projects, each quoted from a note and checked like the weekly preparation's. Suggested tasks show at the top of Tasks and suggested projects at the top of Projects, each with Accept, Edit and Skip. Accepting is an agent change, revertable in Changes. What was skipped or accepted isn't suggested again. It reuses the weekly preparation's gathering, checking and accept actions where it can.
title: Finding tasks and projects in the vault

consequences: Editing the callout means using another editor; Fix restores the last text Brainstead saw, which may be the one another app put there.
context: A system note (the To Do list, Scratchpad, bookmarks, saved searches, canonical docs, the summaries' notes) opens with a 'This is a system note' callout other features look for; a user or an assistant could break it.
decision: Brainstead's editor won't change the callout (changes touching it are filtered out, text joined to its edges refused, a lock shows why); an assistant's change to it is held whoever started it; Knowledge health remembers each callout seen intact and, when one goes, flags it with a safe fix that puts it back. Other apps can still change the file.
title: System notes' headers are locked

consequences: The changes tool refuses accept with a reason; the user accepts the rest on the Changes screen.
context: Code review found an assistant could accept its own held changes through the MCP changes tool, including Templates/ and runnable-code holds.
decision: Over MCP, accept and accept_run work only in an attended session and only for changes held because a check failed. A change held because it touches Templates/ or adds runnable code is accepted only in the app by the user. An unattended session can't accept anything.
title: Assistants accept held changes only when the user is there

consequences: The screens' own edits stay as they are; only assistant-initiated ones are recorded.
context: The MCP task, Inbox, project and bookmark tools wrote directly, so they had no Revert in Changes and ignored unattended, contrary to D-20261005-03.
decision: Every assistant edit to tasks, the Inbox and projects is submitted through changes.rs like a page edit: recorded with Revert, and held when unattended and a check fails.
title: Assistant task, Inbox and project edits go through Changes

consequences: Other renames and trashes still apply at once.
context: Renames and moves to the Trash apply at once, but a change to Templates/ is always held; the two rules overlapped.
decision: Templates win: a rename or trash of a file in Templates/, or a rename whose link rewrites change a template, is held for the user.
title: Renames and trashes touching Templates/ are held

consequences: Assistants can retire them when the user asks; the tool says what it removed.
context: Every screen action needs an MCP equivalent; Retire them in Moving over had none.
decision: Add an MCP tool for retiring the previous app's skills and scripts, named as the screen names it.
title: Moving over's Retire has an MCP tool

consequences: Each assistant task edit is one change with Revert and a ⌘Z entry. The weekly_suggestion tool still writes directly through weeklyPrep.ts choice().run().
context: D-20261005-10 needed these MCP tools to go through changes.rs, but their edits were worked out by writing (task commands, settleInboxItem). A clarify touches two notes (To Do list and a project).
decision: The window works out the edit without writing (src/tasksq/edits.ts, plus change_task_line and change_project_note in src-tauri/src/changes.rs) and submits instructions: lines (at, old, new), add_task, append, properties, page, trash. changes_submit_many holds every change of a batch when any is held, else applies them in order. A capture is marked done only once its changes are made. The screens' own edits are unchanged; clarifyItem (used by the weekly review's suggestions) still writes directly.
title: Assistant task, Inbox and project edits are line instructions, submitted together

consequences: A held whole-page rewrite keeps the page's hash as before and Accept refuses if it changed since; one held without it is refused too.
context: D-20261005-09: assistants may accept only changes held for a failed check.
decision: Change.for_user keeps why only the user can accept it (a template, runnable code, a job set to hold, a rename or trash touching Templates/). change_accept and changes_accept_all take assistant: true from the MCP changes tool and refuse those; for changes held before the field, the reason is worked out again on the page as it is. The MCP server refuses accept and accept_run once any call in the session said unattended.
title: Why a change is the user's to accept is kept on it

consequences: Re-adding it needs the user to reverse D-20261005-05.
context: A review asked to re-add propose_edit as an alias of edit_page for one release, as the agent-changes plan said.
decision: Not re-added: D-20261005-05 already decided no aliases while the MCP server is unreleased.
title: propose_edit stays gone

consequences: A test checks every tool lists it. weekly_start_over and moving_over's retire describe that they're refused once a call said unattended.
context: The MCP instructions ask an unwatched session to pass unattended: true on every call, but only the change tools listed it and every schema sets additionalProperties false, so strict clients could reject it on reading tools.
decision: tool() in src-tauri/mcp/src/lib.rs adds an optional unattended boolean to every tool's schema. Any call that says it marks the whole session unattended, as before.
title: Every MCP tool takes unattended

consequences: Help (sources, guide-wiki, review) describes images as flagged. Images stay ingestible as in D-20261004-20; only its always-queued rule is replaced.
context: D-20261004-20 said changes from an image always go to the review queue. Since D-20261005-03 the review queue is Changes, where changes are made at once and held only by exception, and the in-app help disagreed with itself about images.
decision: Every change from an image carries the check 'It rests on text read from an image'. Like any failed check, it is made at once and flagged when the user started it, and held when a scheduled run (the nightly check) made it. A change from an image is never dropped for a quote missing from the OCR text; other sources drop a change only when none of its quotes is found, and keep one with some missing, flagged.
title: Image changes are flagged by a check, not always queued

consequences: Fidelity depends on the Quick Look previewers on the machine; on other platforms platform::quick_look opens the file's app. Embedding Quick Look in the pane is possible later.
context: docx-preview drew Word files poorly (boxes for bullets, wrong fonts) and PowerPoint and Excel showed only text; no web renderer draws decks well, and Docker-based converters (Gotenberg) are too heavy a dependency for a desktop app. macOS Quick Look, with the previewers Office installs, shows them well.
decision: A Word, PowerPoint or Excel source shows the text Brainstead reads from it (what search, ingest and quotes use), by slide or sheet, with a Quick Look button and Space opening the system Quick Look panel (file_quick_look, platform::quick_look) and Open in its app. docx-preview is removed. Quick Look changes nothing, so there's no MCP tool for it; assistants read the same text with read_section.
title: Office sources: extracted text in the pane, Quick Look for how they look

consequences: make dev still shows neither switch; a register that needs approval shows off until the user approves it in System Settings
context: The switch was only in Settings › General, and hidden in the installed app; keepr and two-edged-sword have it in their menu-bar window and decide availability from the bundle
decision: Brainstead's menu-bar window has an Open at login switch next to Settings › General's; shown only from a .app bundle; only SMAppService Enabled counts as on; RequiresApproval opens System Settings › Login Items. Not an MCP tool: the MCP server exposes no app settings
title: Open at login: in the menu-bar window too, behaving as in the sibling apps

consequences: A due date no longer overrides a later defer date on Today; it shows again on the defer day, in Overdue or Due as its due date says
context: Today listed due and overdue tasks whatever their defer date, so deferring a task due today to tomorrow left it under Due today; the user expected it to go
decision: todayRows leaves out any open task whose defer (scheduled) date is after today; that covers Today, the sidebar and menu-bar counts and MCP's today list
title: A task deferred past today is off Today, even when due or overdue

consequences: A held note (scheduled or failing a check) still gets the offer when accepted in Changes. Undo is per step via Changes and the Trash, not one Undo for the chain. Sources has no row selection, so batches run from the meeting screen's ticks
context: Making a meeting note took the meeting screen, Draft, then a per-note offer to ingest and trash; the earlier new-meeting-note and multi-new-meeting-notes skills did it end to end and only asked when unsure
decision: Make a meeting note (Sources row Meeting note button with Ingest on its menu, right-click menu, Inbox M) drafts, makes, ingests the note then trashes the transcript when Brainstead is sure (confident, date not the capture day, no note of that name); otherwise it opens the meeting screen at the question. Draft and Draft all there follow through the same way, one toast per batch. Settings meetingIngest/meetingTrash default on; with both off the old offer shows. Order is note, ingest, trash; a failure keeps the transcript. MCP meeting_note follows the same settings. Ingest-on-arrival skips transcripts
title: Meeting notes in one step: ingest and trash the transcript by default

consequences: Prompts are bigger for big pages (up to 24k chars a page). Not done: weekly prep still only reads notes dated this week (running notes left out), meeting drafts and draft reply are uncapped, contradictions don't split one page larger than a batch
context: Ingest showed the model each wiki page's first 4,000 characters; real hub pages are 150 KB with a long sources: list first, so it saw neither the outline, the summary nor the newest sections, appended at the bottom, and could rewrite sections it hadn't seen. Find tasks, weekly prep, contradictions, the ingest catalogue, Ask's next-message suggestion and MCP read_section had the same kind of cut
decision: core pageview: view(page, budget) drops sources:, shows a page that fits whole, else every heading with the opening, summing-up (Current state, Summary, Status…) and newest sections in full; ingest's plan drops a change that rewrites a section not shown whole; new sections go above a closing See also. excerpt(note, n) keeps a note's start (a quarter) and end (the rest) for find, weekly prep and MCP read_section without headings; Ask's suggestion keeps the end of turns; weekly prep keeps the newest notes; contradictions get pages without sources:; the ingest catalogue drops summaries then descriptions before cutting. Ingest pages share 120k chars, 6k–24k each
title: Models see long pages as an outline, never a head cut

consequences: A second request waits for the first instead of running alongside. Sources of the same day keep the order asked. An undated file copied in recently sorts by its copy date
context: Each ingest request ran its own thread, so two requests (two screens, an assistant's calls, the nightly check) changed the same wiki page at once; and an agent passing sources in any order let an older source have the last word
decision: src-tauri/src/ingest.rs: every ingest and meeting-note run goes through one app-wide queue (QUEUE), one at a time; what waits is sorted by the source's day (core ingest::source_day: a YYYY-MM-DD or a written-out date in its name, else the file's modified day; a meeting note's own date), stable for the same day. All paths are checked before any run is announced. A run stopped while waiting is marked stopped without starting; runs left queued or running by a closed app are marked stopped at start (settle_stale). MCP start_run's description says so
title: One ingest queue, oldest source first

consequences: No model bulk migration. Until it's built, ingest still writes sections as now (with D-20261006-04's page view and placement fixes)
context: Ingest let the model choose where text goes; pages had sections below See also, Current state at the bottom, repeated entries for one source and dated sections out of order. A survey of 307 entity/concept pages found 2,028 dated sections (71% day-level, 93% citing a vault source), so most can be reshaped mechanically
decision: Keep markdown. Every wiki page: opening text, Current state, topical sections, Timeline (### YYYY-MM-DD — title entries, one per source, keyed by a source comment), See also. Ingest returns entry / current_state / topical section and the app places them; claims are kept per page. The migration is core::pageshape (pure, invariant-checked, idempotent) applied as one Changes run, auto pages by script, review pages with the user, a cheap model only for single headings on request. Plan in archive/wiki-page-shape.md, not built yet; its open questions go to the user first
title: Wiki pages get one shape, owned by the app; migrated by script

consequences: pageview's newest entries are the top of Timeline; reshape and Patch::Entry insert by date in descending order
context: Open question 1 of the wiki page shape plan (D-20261006-06): order of ### entries under ## Timeline
decision: Timeline entries are sorted newest first; within a day, by the order they were written. Month (YYYY-MM) and half/quarter (YYYY-H1, YYYY-Q3) entries sort after the days of that period
title: Wiki Timeline is newest first

consequences: The files are app-owned data in the vault, written through changes.rs like any other vault write; other tools can read them; a rename or trash of a page must carry its claims file
context: Open question 2 of the wiki page shape plan: where ingest's checked claims are stored
decision: One JSON file per page at wiki/.claims/<folder>/<page>.json in the vault, so they sync and survive the app
title: Wiki claims are kept in the vault

consequences: The optional archive split is not built
context: Open question 3 of the wiki page shape plan: move old Timeline entries of big pages to a '<Page> (archive)' page
decision: No. Every Timeline entry stays on its page; pageview's outline handles long pages
title: No archive split for long wiki pages

consequences: A new item in the plan, after the migration; it is a model run, so it goes through changes.rs with its checks, and the user reviews a sample before the whole run
context: Open question 4 of the wiki page shape plan: 203 entity/concept pages have no summing-up section
decision: After the scripted migration, write a Current state for each page that lacks one with the cheap model (Haiku), from the page's opening and newest Timeline entries only, as one run in Changes (one change per page, revertable). About 200 short calls
title: Missing Current state sections written now with Haiku

consequences: It shows in reading view and counts as a link (backlinks, graph). The reshape invariant allows this one added line per entry; the key is read from that line, so a hand edit to it changes the entry's key
context: Open question 5 of the wiki page shape plan: how an entry records the note or source it came from (it keys the entry: one source, one entry per page)
decision: A visible line right under the entry heading: 'Source: [[<note or source>]]', not an HTML comment
title: Timeline entry source is a visible Source line

consequences: Those pages reshape by themselves; the As of line is an added line in the report
context: The page shape dry run found 7 pages whose summing heading carries a date (Status (Apr 2026), Current state (w/e 18 Sep 2026))
decision: When a page has one summing section and its heading's extra words say when, reshape renames it Current state and puts 'As of <those words>.' as its first line; extra words without a date still need the user. A heading counts as summing with extra words only when a bracket or separator follows the name (not 'Status of teams')
title: Dated summing headings become Current state with an As of line

consequences: No Suggest button for single headings yet (optional in the plan); review pages are fixed by hand or reshaped as proposed. The fixture vault has an out-of-shape page (wiki/entities/Acme Pilot.md) for the health-page-shape scene, linked from the lint overlay so the frozen lint parity still holds
context: Item 5 of the wiki page shape plan (D-20261006-06): the migration applied in the app
decision: core lint gains the page-shape check (More checks): one item per entity/concept page not in the shape, safe when reshape needs nobody, else its reasons; it is left out of Fix safe issues. Reshape pages (health_reshape) applies the safe pages, or named ones as proposed, each one change (origin lint, label Reshape pages, run reshape-<id>) with one log.md line per run. Changes gains Revert all for a run (changes_revert_all; MCP changes revert_run). MCP page_shape reads the dry run locally; reshape_pages acts through the app
title: Reshape pages: a Knowledge health check and fix, one Changes run, Revert all

consequences: One entry per source per date holds for ingest (item 7); a source with entries on several dates still needs a rule there
context: After Reshape pages on the real vault, 16 pages needed the user: 14 had two entries citing one note (mostly two topics from one meeting), one had Status (Mar 2026) and Status (Apr 2026), one (a milestones table under ## Timeline) is renamed by hand
