decision: Entries citing the same source with the same date become one: the first keeps its heading, each later one follows under its title as a #### heading (its own headings a level down), its Source line dropped. Entries from one source on different dates stay for the user (often a real later follow-up). When every summing section is dated and one is newest, it becomes Current state with an As of line and the others become Timeline entries
title: Page shape: one source's entries on one date merge; of dated summing sections the newest is Current state

consequences: A source with entries on several dates (4 real pages) gets its first entry replaced on re-ingest; claims are still thrown away until item 8
context: Item 7 of the wiki page shape plan (D-20261006-06): ingest still let the model pick a section to rewrite
decision: The ingest answer per page is entry {date, title, body} (filed in the Timeline by date, newest first, with a Source line; the same source again replaces its entry), current_state (the whole section, placed after the opening), and section {heading, content} (topical only, rewritten only if shown whole, new ones above the Timeline). Old answers (section name + content) still apply. A Source line the model writes in an entry's body is dropped. pageview shows a shaped page's Timeline from the top. Write Current state accepts links to pages in the vault. evals: re-ingest a source (twice) and a new current state; make evals' cargo run has default-run
title: Ingest gives entries; the app places them

consequences: A change can carry a second file (the page's claims). Pages with no kept claims are checked as before
context: Item 8 of the wiki page shape plan (claims kept in wiki/.claims/, D-20261006-08): how the claims file is recorded, and how contradictions use it
decision: An ingest's claims file is written as part of its page's change: one Changes row, and Revert restores both files. Re-ingesting a source replaces that source's claims on the page. Contradictions keep extracting claims from pages and add the kept claims alongside them, without duplicates
title: Kept claims: one Changes row with the page; contradictions use them alongside extraction

consequences: facts answers only from claims ingest kept since claims shipped. No claims-only kind of change in Changes. If seeding is wanted later, it needs that kind of change first, and only sourced claims (in a Timeline entry with a Source line) can be seeded.
context: Item 9 of the wiki page shape plan: seed kept claims (wiki/.claims/) from the contradictions cache, no model. The cache had 751 claims on 383 pages, 731 still quoting their page, but only about 171 sit in a Timeline entry with a Source line; the rest (opening text, topical sections, Current state) have no source to file them under. Changes can't record a claims-only change: one that leaves the page text the same is refused.
decision: Don't seed. Kept claims start with ingests made after D-20261006-16. The contradiction check already uses the cache's claims alongside kept ones, so nothing is lost there.
title: Claims are not seeded from the contradictions cache

consequences: Reshaping stays a user-started Knowledge health fix. A summing heading given to edit_page on a shaped page becomes Current state, not a section of its own name.
context: Item 10 of the wiki page shape plan. Pages are also edited in other editors, which can put them out of the shape; and a section edit (edit_page, a change's section) added a heading it didn't find at the end, above See also, which on a shaped page lands below the Timeline.
decision: The nightly check surveys the entity and concept pages and says in its summary how many aren't in the shape and how many Reshape pages can do by itself; it doesn't reshape them itself. On an entity or concept page a section edit with a heading the page lacks puts a topical one above the Timeline and a summing one (Summary, Status...) as the Current state (pageshape::with_section); other pages and headings the page has behave as before.
title: Keeping pages in the page shape: nightly counts drift, edits place new sections

consequences: An ignored issue without a page stays ignored until Show again. MCP lint still lists ignored issues (it runs outside the app). Per-check actions (Link from, Still true) can come later.
context: Checks such as orphan pages and stale pages showed amber issues with no button, which the user found frustrating.
decision: Every issue that isn't a safe fix and whose check has no buttons of its own gets Ignore: kept in the app's health.json with the page's version, left out of the list and the count until the page changes; the check shows how many it's ignoring, with Show again. MCP ignore_issue does both. Advisory checks (stale pages, uncited claims, no Current state) get a grey icon, and no-current-state joins the core's advisory list so the sidebar count and the screen agree.
title: Knowledge health: Ignore for issues with nothing to fix; advisory checks are grey

consequences: Supersedes D-20261006-19's 'MCP lint still lists ignored issues' while the app is open. Saved searches have no delete or rename because the screen has none. Deleting from the Trash for good and emptying it stay out of MCP.
context: An audit found screen actions with no MCP tool (Contradictions, doing the Weekly review, Knowledge health's per-issue buttons, Ask's chats, saved task lists, settings, Sources' Import, New template), and lint disagreeing with the screen: no system-note header or uncited checks, ignored issues and dismissed duplicates still listed, no sign of safe fixes or uncounted checks, silent truncation at 40.
decision: New tools weekly_step, chats, health_issue, contradictions, task_lists, settings, import_sources and create_template, named after the buttons they press; trash restore takes to, list_tasks takes a saved list, saved_searches takes search's layer names, run_status and stop_run cover find_tasks and write_current_state, ignore_issue refuses checks with their own buttons. lint asks the app (health.lint) when it's running and only falls back to the core's checks when it isn't; each check says its id and whether it's counted, safe fixes are marked, overflow is counted. settings changes an allow-list only: the vault, Read-only and excluded folders stay the user's. create_template is always held (it's in Templates/), and a new template doesn't get created-by: assistant (proposals::gets_mark), which every note made from it would inherit. Write Current state, Reshape pages and Link to… pass unattended so a scheduled session's failing change is held.
title: MCP covers every screen action: eight more tools; lint reads the app's report when it's open

consequences: Supersedes D-20261006-20's note that saved searches have no delete. saved_searches' description no longer claims a taken name is replaced: add_smart_list refuses it.
context: Saved searches (Me. Smart Lists.md) could only be removed by editing the note, and MCP's saved_searches had no delete (D-20261006-20 left it out because the screen had none).
decision: Each saved search in Search's side list has an x that deletes its line from Me. Smart Lists.md (core lists::remove_smart_list, command smart_list_delete), undoable with ⌘Z; saved_searches takes delete with name. Renaming stays an edit of the note.
title: Saved searches can be deleted, in Search and through MCP

consequences: A test fails if a tool gains offset without being in PAGED or the other way round. Lists inside one item (a page's shape report, lint's per-check items) say how many more instead of paging.
context: Tool results over 30,000 characters are cut, and listing tools either had no cap (the Trash, chats, held changes, backlinks, the Inbox, projects, bookmarks, transcripts, contradictions) or cut silently (a day's activity at 80, the graph at 200, page shape at 40 or 30).
decision: The 14 listing tools (PAGED in src-tauri/mcp/src/lib.rs) all take limit, offset and query, and each reply starts with how many there are, which rows are shown and the offset for the next page (pagedRows in src/mcpActions.ts, page_of in the server). query keeps rows with all its words. Defaults: 50 rows, 30 for log.md and made changes, 20 contradictions (10 claims each), 80 for a day's files, 200 graph links.
title: Every MCP listing tool pages the same way

consequences: 69 tools, up from 59. Sessions and scripts that called trash, or the list actions of changes, chats, bookmarks, saved_searches, contradictions, suggestions, automated_tools, task_lists, settings or moving_over status, now call the list_ tool; the refusal says which. A new listing tool returns listed()'s {text, structured} from src/mcpActions.ts and gets an entry in outputs() in the server. A test keeps the instructions under 2,000 characters and every parameter described.
context: A check of the MCP server against Anthropic's guidance on writing tools and the MCP spec found: argument errors were JSON-RPC errors the model couldn't act on; the instructions were over the ~2,000 characters Claude Code keeps, cutting the held-change rule; tools mixing reads and changes couldn't be marked read-only; several parameters had no description; listings were text only and only list_tasks had a detail switch.
decision: Each read of something a tool also changes is a tool of its own, marked read-only: list_changes, list_chats, list_trash, list_bookmarks, list_saved_searches, list_contradictions, list_suggestions, list_automated_tools, list_task_lists, list_settings; trash became list_trash and restore_from_trash; moving_over only retires (app_status says whether there's anything to retire). The change tools refuse the read actions and the read tools the change ones, before the app hears of it. Only an unknown tool is a JSON-RPC error; bad arguments are isError results. Instructions stay under 2,000 characters. Every parameter has a description. The main listings (search, list_tasks, list_inbox, list_projects, list_trash, list_changes, activity, list_chats, list_bookmarks, list_transcripts) declare an outputSchema and give structuredContent as well as text; search, list_projects, list_changes, activity and graph give a short line a row unless detail is true (a boolean, as list_tasks already had). stop_run, the tools that remove things (bookmarks, saved_searches, task_lists, automated_tools, chats, suggestions, weekly_suggestion's skip, health_issue's move_to_trash) are destructive; settings, stop_run, update_project and task_lists are idempotent. No aliases for the old names (D-20261005-05).
title: MCP follows Anthropic's tool guidance: read tools apart, errors as results, data and detail

consequences: To move a project's work between the lines, change its area. Sessions in folders not named after a project still rely on the model reading their messages.
context: The daily summary's model guessed each session's domain, so a personal project's sessions landed under Work some days and Personal on others.
decision: The summary inputs list every project note (done ones too) with its area; area Personal is Personal, any other area is Work. A session whose folder name matches a project (letters and digits, case ignored) gets a Project: line. The workflows say the project's area settles the domain.
title: Summaries split Work and Personal by project area

consequences: A user who never set a time now runs at 09:00. The kept names are the only nightly left, and must stay unless their data is migrated.
context: The nightly check ran at 02:10 while the laptop was asleep, so it started late and stalled; the user asked for it to be called the daily check, run by default at 09:00.
decision: Daily check everywhere: UI, help, docs, MCP (start_run/stop_run take daily_check, still accept nightly), code (daily_check.rs, daily_check_* commands, daily-check-changed event). New runs' Changes groups are daily-check-…; old nightly-… groups are labelled Daily check too. Default time 09:00. Kept for existing data: the settings keys nightlyEnabled and nightlyTime and the state file nightly.json.
title: Nightly check renamed Daily check, default 09:00

consequences: Editing a claim's line brings it back, as a new issue. Another check whose issue is one whole line can join LINE_KEYED.
context: An ignored issue came back whenever its page changed at all, and wiki pages change often (ingests, the daily check), so ignored claims with no citation kept returning; one that dropped out of its check for a run lost its ignore for good.
decision: Claims with no citation (lint::LINE_KEYED) stay ignored while their line reads the same, whatever else changes on the page; their ignore is kept while the page still has the line, even when the check doesn't list it for a while. Other issues still come back when their page changes.
title: Ignored uncited claims last while their line does

consequences: Old MCP settings key names stop working (nobody else used them). Each item lands with docs, help and tests.
context: The 2026-10-07 consistency audit found screen actions and settings with no MCP tool, and tool names that differ from the screen.
decision: Plan in archive/mcp-parity.md (local). Summary undo goes through changes revert, not a new action; unsaved drafts stay with the screen; the settings tool's key names are replaced by the screen's (dailyCheck, summaries.*), no aliases, stored keys unchanged; Rebuild index gets a rebuild_index tool.
title: MCP parity plan for the screens' remaining actions

consequences: Renames break old settings files: anyone else's settings for a renamed key reset to the default. Revisit once the app has outside users.
context: D-20261007-02 kept nightlyEnabled, nightlyTime and nightly.json, and D-20261007-04 kept the stored settings keys, for existing data; the user says the app isn't publicly used yet.
decision: Every name follows the screen, stored names included (settings keys, state files, Changes group ids, MCP arguments and run names), with no aliases or fallbacks in code. The user's own app data is moved over once, by hand, when a rename lands. Supersedes the kept names in D-20261007-02 and D-20261007-04.
title: Proper names everywhere, no aliases, before public use

consequences: A client pages Changes with one offset. Reading bookmarks for triage needs no confirmation, as every read tool.
context: list_changes paged only held changes (offset forced to 0 for made ones), and triage_bookmarks was a Run tool that only read without items.
decision: list_changes pages one list in display order, held first then made newest first; structured held and made each carry their own total and matching and the shared offset and next_offset. list_bookmarks gives Triage's untouched days (days, stale); triage_bookmarks requires items and only runs the model, and is no longer paged.
title: MCP: Changes pages as one list; bookmark triage's read is list_bookmarks

consequences: Old settings, files and groups are not read: the user's own data is moved by hand once. Old MCP argument names now fail.
context: D-20261007-05 asked for every name to follow the screen with no aliases; the audit of settings keys, app-data files, Changes groups and MCP fields found more than the listed ones.
decision: Settings: dailyCheckEnabled, dailyCheckTime, summariesHere, holdSummaries, summaries {dailyEnabled, dailyTime, weeklyEnabled, weeklyDay, weeklyTime}, weeklyReview {day, time}, jobModels.summaries (was reviews), movingOver (was switchover, with its otherSummaries item). App data: daily-check.json, summaries/ (was reviews/, with automated.json, state.json, undo/). Summary runs' Changes groups are summary-…; the daily check's daily-check-…; no fallbacks for nightly-… or daily-review labels. MCP: no nightly, daily_review or weekly_review run names; projects take done_looks_like and status completed, mapped to the note's outcome and status done at the boundary; fix_name takes written_as and correct_spelling; doc_check takes document, governing_document and mode version_in_force or earlier_feedback. Left: the vault's own names, origin kind review (shared with the weekly review), substitutions.json's wrong/right (the previous app's corrections format), internal command and module names.
title: Stored and MCP names follow the screen (2026-10-07 renames)

consequences: No new MCP action for summary undo. Recent runs shows undone after a revert in Changes; its Undo button goes.
context: MCP parity item 2: run_status gives each summary run's change so changes revert undoes it. A summary's block was already written (or held) as an agent change in the run's group (summary-…), but reverting it in Changes left the run not undone and its Undo file behind.
decision: run_status lists the last eight summary runs with the id and state of the change in their group. Reverting a summary's change in Changes (origin kind review, run summary-…) marks the run undone and removes its undo file (reviews::reverted_in_changes), so Changes' Revert and Recent runs' Undo end the same.
title: Summary runs undone through Changes

consequences: settings' value accepts null. Model choices are looked up again when no assistant was found before.
context: Items 1, 3, 5, 8 of archive/mcp-parity.md left the argument shapes open.
decision: open takes transcript (screen meeting), thread (reply) and document (doc_check), named as start_run meeting_note, draft_reply and doc_check name them; a transcript must be one list_transcripts knows, the others resolve in the vault. list_inbox suggest asks the model about the first 20 rows of the page shown, as Suggest for all (first 20) does, with the active projects. settings: choice settings (spellLanguage, speechVoice, docStyle, docAccent, docTheme) and model settings (askModel, jobModels.<job>) take one of the choices list_settings gives, by id or label; null puts back the default choice (As macOS, System voice, As the app, As new chats); speechRate is 0.5 to 2 in the slider's 0.05 steps; openAtLogin is macOS's login item, offered only where macOS manages it. The model jobs list moved to askState.MODEL_JOBS for Settings and the tool. rebuild_index does nothing while the index is being built.
title: MCP parity: argument shapes for the 2026-10-07 items

consequences: An assistant can move notes to the Trash and restore them, but only the user empties it or deletes for good.
context: The MCP parity re-audit found no tool for Trash's Empty the Trash and Delete for good.
decision: Left out of the MCP on purpose: they can't be undone, and every other change an assistant makes can be reverted in Changes or restored from the Trash. Part 2 of archive/mcp-parity.md covers the re-audit's other gaps.
title: Emptying the Trash and Delete for good stay with the screen

consequences: Old argument names (save_chat title, automated_tools folder and opening) now fail, with no aliases. Ticking Moving over's items and retiring stay refused in an unattended session. A capture or example note is revertable in Changes, not by Quick capture's or the button's direct write.

title: MCP parity part 6: the sixth audit's fixes and shapes

consequences: Drift is prevented at the source; a gap that slips through is fixed when its feature next changes.
context: Six full re-audits each reread the whole app (about 80-190k tokens) and found fewer gaps each time (20, 20, 12, 4, 3), mostly where a tool reimplemented what its screen does.
decision: After the seventh pass, stop whole-app parity audits. Later checks cover only code changed since the last one. Tools call the screen's own functions instead of reimplementing them (CLAUDE.md rule). archive/mcp-parity.md is marked complete with any remaining gaps listed as known.
title: No more full MCP parity re-audits

consequences: Every MCP write now goes through Changes. weekprep_link returns the change's outcome rather than its id, so a held link is reported as held. Changes shows a Restored from the Trash chip.
context: The seventh audit (archive/mcp-parity.md items 70-74) found restore_from_trash writing to the vault outside Changes, Find suggestions and weekly review links accepted unattended being applied even when a check failed, an unattended contradictions save not held, start_run weekly_summary taking a week that hadn't ended, and the Inbox's Done not adding a recurring task's next occurrence.
decision: An assistant's restore is a change with a new Restore instruction (kind restore, page = where it goes back): checked as a new page with the trashed file's text, so a restore into Templates/ or of runnable code is always held; Revert moves it back to the Trash. The screen's own Restore stays direct. find_decide and weekprep_link take unattended, giving their change's origin trigger scheduled; restore_from_trash and contradictions get the session origin like the other writing tools. weekly_summary refuses a week whose Sunday hasn't passed (Target::ended). The Inbox's Done uses toggleTaskEdit via inboxActions.doneNow.
title: MCP parity part 7: restores, suggestions and contradictions reports go through Changes with the session's trigger

consequences: No per-transcript Confirm needed for a batch. The MCP is unchanged: start_run meeting_note already takes the date explicitly, which is its confirmation.
context: Ticked transcripts dated only with their capture day each needed Confirm clicked before Draft all would run.
decision: Draft all opens a dialog listing each ticked transcript's date, editable, marking capture-day ones; its Draft all button sets them all as confirmed. A Tick all box above the list ticks every transcript shown.
title: Meeting notes: Draft all confirms every date in one dialog

consequences: No MCP tool: edit_page already changes or removes an embed's text.
context: Edit hid an image behind its markdown whenever the cursor was on its line, and there was no way to resize or remove one without editing the text. View ignored Obsidian's |400 width.
decision: An image stays drawn unless the selection is inside its markdown; double-click puts the cursor there. Hover shows a frame, four corner handles that write the width as Obsidian does (![[pic.png|400]], ![alt|400](pic.png); height dropped to keep proportions), and a trash button that removes the embed (its line too when alone) but leaves the file; Knowledge health's unused-images check offers to trash the file. View honours the same size syntax (imageSize/setImageWidth in src/md/wikilinks.ts). Paste reads clipboard items as well as files.
title: Images in Edit: drawn on the cursor's line, resized by handles, removed by a trash button

consequences: Scenes focus and focus-images check it.
context: Asked for Two-edged Sword's focus mode: the open document full window with only the essential buttons.
decision: ⌘. (Note menu: Focus Mode, also a top-bar button) hides the sidebar, side pane and details line, centres the text a size larger, and keeps only the title, Read aloud, Text size and Exit focus. View, Edit and Source all work in it. Esc (unless something else took it), ⌘. again, or leaving the doc screen ends it (src/focus.ts). MCP open takes focus.
title: Focus mode (⌘.) for notes, wiki pages and sources

consequences: A warm run takes about 15 s; the first after a clean is a few minutes. The check folder doubles cargo's disk use.
context: make check had grown to several minutes, ran every step in series, and waited on cargo's lock while make dev was building.
decision: tools/check.py runs rust (fmt, tests, clippy), tsc, eslint, vitest and format groups in parallel, printing each when done; cargo uses src-tauri/target/check; Vitest uses pool vmThreads (15 s to 5 s) with waitFor at 5 s and tests at 20 s for a busy machine; eslint and prettier use their caches; brainstead-core is optimised for make dev but not for tests.
title: make check runs its groups side by side in its own cargo folder

consequences: Click and double-click on an image in Edit keep their meaning. Small images aren't enlarged past their natural size.
context: The user wanted to click an image in View and Edit to see it full size. In Edit a click already selects an image for its resize handles and a double-click shows its markdown.
decision: A click on an image in View shows it full size over the window (src/ImageViewer.tsx), fitted to it, a click toggling actual size, Escape or a click beside it closing it. In Edit an expand button shows on hover beside the remove button (the user chose it over ⌘-click or a plain click). MCP open takes image, by name or path, to do the same.
title: Images open full size: a click in View, an expand button in Edit

consequences: Anyone who distributes a changed copy must share its source under the GPL; private and internal use is unaffected.
context: Before making the repo public the licence was reviewed: GPL keeps forks' improvements open; MIT or Apache would allow closed reuse.
decision: Keep GPL-3.0-or-later. The GitHub topics, obsidian-compatible among them, stay as set.
title: Brainstead stays GPL-3.0-or-later as a public repo

consequences: Rows are role=row divs, not buttons, so they can hold the pencil. Renaming to an existing area merges.
context: Asked for a collapsible, remembered projects tree, areas editable in the tree, and an edit button on projects (in place, or the note in edit mode).
decision: Area bands fold (kept in viewMemory as projects:folded). A pencil on the band renames the area on every project under it, any status (areaProjects, shared with MCP rename_area), as one undo (projects_set_area). Edit, on the row and the page, opens the note in Edit (editDoc); open gets edit. Outcome and area already edit in place on the page, so Edit covers the rest of the note.
title: Projects: areas fold and rename in the list, Edit opens the project note in Edit

consequences: Pages must be set to deploy from GitHub Actions. Screenshots in site/img are copies to refresh after make screenshots. A custom domain means updating the canonical URL, Open Graph tags, structured data and sitemap together.
context: A product page for GitHub Pages was wanted. Pages can serve only a branch's root or docs/, and docs/ holds the markdown docs.
decision: The page lives in site/ as plain HTML, CSS and JS, light only, using WebP copies of the docs screenshots, and .github/workflows/pages.yml deploys it to waynetd777.github.io/brainstead on changes to site/.
title: Product page in site/, published by GitHub Actions

consequences: A docs-only or page-only commit gets no CI run, so make check locally stays the gate. A new folder of app code is covered without changes, since the list names what to skip.
context: Actions had been switched off because CI builds used up the account's GitHub limits, which also stopped the product page deploying.
decision: ci.yml ignores pushes and pull requests that change only docs/, site/, _sift/, archive/, README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE or the Pages workflow, and can be started by hand; Actions is on again so pages.yml deploys site/.
title: CI runs only for app changes

consequences: The github.io address redirects to it. Search Console needs a property for the new address. Supersedes the address in D-20261008-02.
context: The product page was at waynetd777.github.io/brainstead; the project now has its own domain.
decision: The page is served at https://brainstead.davies.co.za/, a CNAME to waynetd777.github.io set as the repo's Pages custom domain. The canonical URL, link-preview tags, structured data, sitemap, README, About's Website button and docs/development.md name it.
title: Product page on brainstead.davies.co.za

consequences: Choosing Stay in the leave dialog keeps the old copy running with the update already on disk. Losing the signing key means no installed copy can update again.
context: tauri-plugin-updater installs the new app in place; AppHandle::restart skips the window's unsaved-edits question and, called on the main thread, the ExitRequested work too.
decision: Install and Restart emits restart-requested; the window runs whenFree (the leave dialog), flushes settings and calls app_restart, which uses request_restart so ExitRequested saves the window state and stops running CLIs. It waits while an Ask answer, ingest, daily check, contradiction check, summary, weekly prep, Find or Write Current state is going. Checks run in release builds only, not in --mcp or screenshot scenes; packages are signed by tools/update_files.py, and bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts stays off so builds don't need the key.
title: Updates from GitHub releases restart by the quit road

consequences: Sessions keep working across updates and pick up new tools; clients that ignore list_changed keep the old tool list until restarted. Unix only. A build that execs but then dies at startup (e.g. settings unreadable) ends the session, as a fresh start would. The rate limit's call times aren't handed on.
context: Claude Code sessions run Brainstead --mcp as a stdio server. make install-app (pkill -x Brainstead) and updates replaced the program under them, and pkill killed the servers too, so every session lost its Brainstead tools until restarted.
decision: make install-app quits only the app (osascript quit, then kill what's left that isn't --mcp or Chrome's capture host). The server notices the program file replaced (device, inode, size, mtime, checked every 3 s; taken once the same on two checks and a bundle has its Info.plist) and, with every request read answered (stdin read unbuffered with poll), execv's it with the same arguments and BRAINSTEAD_MCP_RESUME: session id, unattended, what initialize agreed. The new process sends notifications/tools/list_changed and initialize declares tools.listChanged. A failed exec is logged and that file isn't tried again. File identity rather than the build number, so it also works for dev builds and brainstead-mcp.
title: The MCP server execs a new build of itself in place

consequences: The prompt follows the app's theme and type; scenes update-offer, update-downloading and update-message show it. No MCP tool: installing an update isn't something an assistant should do.
context: The updater asked with the system's alert dialogs, which looked unlike the rest of the app, couldn't render release notes or show the download's progress.
decision: updates.rs emits update-offer, update-progress and update-message to the main window, which shows them in src/Update.tsx (the app's Dialog, buttons and markdown) and answers with update_install, update_later or update_skip. The system's dialogs stand in only when there is no main window. A restart held by unsaved edits closes the dialog so the question shows.
title: The update offer is an in-app dialog

consequences: Dragging touches no note and shows nothing in Changes; the order is per machine and other editors and the previous app don't see it.
context: The Projects screen gets drag-and-drop ordering of areas and of projects within an area. Task order lives in the vault as ^rank-N, but projects and areas have no natural place in the vault for an order, and a drag would rewrite several project notes on a synced vault.
decision: The order is a UI setting (projectOrder: areas by name, projects by path), not written to the vault. Areas and projects not yet dragged go after the ordered ones, A-Z; No area stays last. Renames (of a project note or an area) carry their place in the order. Assistants order them through the MCP server with the same setting.
title: Projects and areas: manual order kept in app settings

consequences: A new source action is added once and shows in all three places; clarify_inbox refuses the source actions that are other tools' (meeting, reply) or the assistant's own reading (ask).
context: The Inbox's capture buttons, a Sources row's button and the file menu each decided their own source actions, so a transcript offered different things in each place.
decision: src/sourceActions.ts sourceActions(path, ingested) is the list, leading choice first: a transcript's meeting note, a thread's reply, else Ingest (Re-ingest once ingested), then Ingest into the wiki and Ask about this source. A Sources row shows the lead with every action on its ▾; the file menu lists them; the Inbox starts a capture's choices with them, then its clarify choices (inboxChoices).
title: One list of source actions for the Inbox, Sources and the file menu

consequences: tests/fixtures/meeting/expected.json differs from infer_meeting.py for that one case (freeze.py says so). Two different people sharing a first name, one with a surname in the notes, are told apart only by the transcript's title.
context: Making a meeting note asked whenever the person's existing 1-1 notes used more than one name, counting each note title (with its topic) as a name form, so a transcript titled '11 Theo, Maya' with many '1-1. Theo' notes still stopped at the Meeting notes screen. The previous app's infer_meeting.py asked in the same case.
decision: Only each note's name part (before its first ' - ') counts, for that first name only. When the transcript's name is one of them it's used without asking; only when it's none of several is the user asked, and the screen offers those names to pick.
title: A 1-1's name that existing notes use is taken without asking

consequences: Kept checks are per computer and not in the vault (Save as note is how findings get there). Stopping ends the model call and keeps nothing.
context: A Doc check could take minutes with nothing to show it was working, and its findings were lost on leaving the page, so the same unchanged documents were checked again and again.
decision: doc_check_start runs a check in the background as steps (read the document, read the version in force, compare), shown with times, a running clock and Stop; leaving the page doesn't stop it and a toast says when it's done. Each finished check is kept in the app data folder (doc-checks/), keyed by document, governing document and mode, with the two documents' versions; the screen and the doc_check tool show it again until either document changes (then it's marked stale), unless asked to check again (fresh).
title: Doc check runs in the background and keeps its results

consequences: An unrelated pair costs one small call. Doc check's feedback mode has no second document, so it has no first look; its prompt says to stop when no earlier feedback is found.
context: Doc check compares a document only with the version in force from the register, or with the user's earlier feedback; comparing any two documents was asked for, and comparing two unrelated documents wasted a full model run on both.
decision: Compare is its own screen (A and B, neither in force; Differences or What changed), sharing Doc check's runs, kept results and progress; the sidebar has one Compare entry with two tabs, Doc check and Any two documents. Before a full comparison, both send only each document's first 4,000 characters and ask whether they're about the same thing; if not, the result says so (unrelated) and nothing more is sent. The full prompts also tell the model to stop if, read in full, they turn out unrelated. compare_docs gives assistants the same.
title: Compare: any two documents, beside Doc check, both stopping early on unrelated documents

consequences: Without a search the run buttons act on the whole run as before. A query that finds nothing in the run is refused by the tool rather than acting on the whole run.
context: With a search on, the run's confirmation counted the changes the search showed while the action sent the whole run's group to the backend, so it could accept, reject or revert changes the user couldn't see.
decision: With a search on, a run's Accept all, Reject all, Revert all and ⌘↩ act only on the run's changes the search shows: the screen passes their ids to changes_accept_all / changes_reject_all / changes_revert_all (new optional ids). knowledge.ts runChanges picks them and is shared with the MCP changes tool, whose accept_run, reject_run and revert_run take a query meaning the same. A meeting note's follow-up is offered only for notes that were actually made.
title: A run's Accept all, Reject all and Revert all follow Changes' search

consequences: No change-store rewrites on rename, and it works for renames made anywhere (the app, another editor). A source renamed and re-ingested before an older ingest is reverted isn't followed, which leaves the newer ingest's claims, as wanted. Link to… renames claims only on the pages it relinks.
context: Renaming a source rewrites the source name in claims files, but an ingest change in Changes still records the old name, so its Revert found nothing to take out.
decision: revert_claims resolves the rename rather than renames updating the change store: when the recorded source has no claims in the file, the source whose claims equal (ignoring source) those the change wrote is taken as the same source renamed. A source rename made by a change (Link to…) records Update.from and its revert puts every touched source's set back from the file before.
title: Revert of claims follows a renamed source by content

consequences: Undo puts the area back where it was; projectOrder.areas can hold names no area has until the next drag, which orderedAreas ignores.
context: Undoing an area rename (toast Undo, Cmd-Z, Revert in Changes) edits the projects' area property back, and nothing tells the screens, so the order (settings.projectOrder, D-20261012-01) had already lost the old name's place.
decision: renameInProjectOrder for areas puts the new name just before the old one and keeps the old; a name left over from an earlier rename isn't treated as an area to merge with (callers pass the areas there before the rename); moveInProjectOrder saves only areas that exist, so leftovers go at the next drag. Project notes keep the simple rename, since their undo is a rename back that fileMoved follows.
title: An area rename keeps the old name's place in the Projects order for an undo

consequences: list_transcripts and the exists-already refusal point at ingest_existing.
context: The card's Ingest the existing note had no MCP equivalent.
decision: Its core is keepNote in meetingFlow.ts (followThrough, ingestStart, trashTranscript), called by the card and by start_run meeting_note with ingest_existing: true rather than a new tool; it ignores the capture-day date check, as the card offers it whatever the date.
title: start_run meeting_note ingest_existing is the meeting card's Ingest the existing note

consequences: A note held in Changes keeps its transcript in the Inbox (shown as held) until the offer after accepting it is acted on or the transcript is trashed. captureDone (src/gtd.ts) now reloads every shown Inbox, since marking a capture done isn't a vault change.
context: Starting a transcript's meeting note marked the capture done at once, while the Inbox's Writing note / Note failed rows and the Inbox help promised it stays until the note is made and ingested and can be chosen again if that fails.
decision: Follow the help: meetingFlow marks the transcript done only when the note's ingest finishes (or when the note is made, with ingesting off), and when the after-the-note offer is acted on; a failed or stopped note or ingest leaves it in the Inbox to be chosen again. makeMeetingNotes ignores a transcript already started until its run ends, so pressing M twice, or the button and M, starts one run.
title: A transcript leaves the Inbox once its meeting note is made and ingested

consequences: A change to what the Inbox offers is made in inboxChoices, in prep::fits and in the fixture together, or one of the two tests fails. Suggest now tells the model an unreadable capture is a file.
context: weekly.rs's fits let Suggest (and list_inbox's suggest) propose done or waiting for captures, which the Inbox doesn't offer, and the weekly review's preparation accepted any outcome for any item, while clarify_inbox refused them.
decision: brainstead_core::reviews::prep has inbox_kind (thought, task, transcript, thread, capture, or file for a capture ingest can't read) and fits, used by clarify_suggest and the weekly prep's clarify check; src/inboxActions.ts's suggestKind and inboxChoices are the window's copy. tests/fixtures/inbox-choices.json is the table of kind to choices, with a sample item per kind, checked by a core Rust test and a vitest test.
title: What Suggest may propose for an Inbox item is what the Inbox offers it, from one shared table

consequences: Snap Layouts and system window behaviour work unchanged; the Windows window looks like a Windows app rather than the macOS mock. A custom title bar can come later with the decorum plugin if wanted.
context: The main window's Overlay title bar, hidden title and traffic-light position are macOS-only settings; Windows draws a standard title bar over a layout that reserved space for the traffic lights, and there are no custom window buttons.
decision: On Windows the main window is decorated with the system title bar (tauri.windows.conf.json overrides app.windows) and the frontend zeroes the traffic-light spacing under html[data-platform=windows]. No frameless chrome or custom buttons.
title: Windows uses the native title bar

consequences: Help and docs are written once with macOS glyphs; sentences that explain the mapping must contain no glyphs or they are rewritten too. Native menu accelerators follow the same table.
context: Every shortcut and label was written for macOS: metaKey handlers and glyph labels. Ctrl+Alt is AltGr on many European layouts, and Win+key combinations are reserved by Windows.
decision: On Windows the Command key is Ctrl and Option is Alt; screen shortcuts (Option+Command+digit) are Ctrl+Shift+digit; Option+Command+letter is Ctrl+Alt+letter; the default capture shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+Space. src/platform.ts holds the rule (isMod, isScreenMod, keyLabel) and help text keeps the macOS glyphs, which the drawer and the MCP help tool rewrite on Windows.
title: Windows keyboard mapping

consequences: A CLI that cannot read stdin would need the argument form back; the stdin path is covered by the args tests and a live claude --version test where npm's shim exists.
context: Windows caps a command line at 32,767 characters, and npm .cmd shims refuse arguments with line breaks; doc check sends prompts of up to 150,000 characters and every prompt is multi-line.
decision: ask::args returns a Launch with the prompt on stdin for Claude (-p with no value) and Codex (exec with - as the prompt), on every platform so one code path is tested on both; Copilot and Antigravity keep the prompt argument with a 30,000-character guard on Windows. npm .cmd shims are resolved to the executable or node script they wrap (core::paths::resolve_npm_shim) so cmd.exe is never the parent.
title: Prompts go to Claude and Codex over stdin

consequences: Scheduled jobs run only while the window or the tray icon is up on Windows, which matches what the user sees.
context: macOS keeps the app alive in the Dock after its window closes and reopens it from the Dock; Windows has no Dock, and an app with no window and no tray icon is unreachable.
decision: On Windows, closing the main window quits the app when Show in the menu bar is off, and hides to the tray when it is on. tauri-plugin-single-instance makes a second launch focus the running app on every desktop platform. The Dock-only setting is hidden on Windows.
title: Closing the window quits on Windows when the tray is off

consequences: The large index lives in the roaming profile, acceptable for now; moving it to %LOCALAPPDATA% is a later change. Registration needs no admin rights.
context: Chrome, Edge, Brave and Chromium on Windows find native messaging hosts through HKCU registry keys pointing at a manifest file, not a folder per browser as on macOS; the app's data folder on Windows was already %APPDATA%\Brainstead.
decision: Data stays in %APPDATA%\Brainstead (BRAINSTEAD_DATA overrides). The native host manifest is written under it and registered through HKCU\Software\<vendor>\NativeMessagingHosts\com.wayned.brainstead for each installed browser (winreg). Open at login is the HKCU Run key; rich copy uses arboard.
title: Windows data folder and native host registration

consequences: Windows users see fewer controls rather than broken ones; each follow-up flips one flag in platform_features when it lands.
context: macOS has Quick Look, system spelling and grammar, Read aloud with media keys, Vision OCR, image downscaling for models and WebKit PDF export; each has a Windows equivalent (ISpellChecker, WinRT SpeechSynthesizer, Windows.Media.Ocr, WebView2 PrintToPdf) but each is a feature in itself.
decision: The first Windows port hides those features through the platform_features command (frontend and MCP read it) and implements only what is small: native host registry, open at login, rich copy. The rest are follow-up changes, one per feature.
title: Windows parity scope for the first port

consequences: macOS development is unchanged. Two dev builds can still run side by side on Windows only with separate BRAINSTEAD_DATA folders and the plugin's lock, which is per identifier.
context: D-20261008-11 said tauri-plugin-single-instance runs on every desktop platform. On macOS the plugin locks a socket named after the app identifier, so make dev would quit and focus the installed app; LaunchServices already stops a second copy there.
decision: The single-instance plugin is registered on Windows and Linux only, skipped in screenshot scenes, and shows the main window on a second launch. On Windows a close with Show in the menu bar off sends quit-requested, so unsaved edits are asked about before the app quits.
title: Single instance only off macOS

consequences: No rewriting of authors or who fields before a merge; fixtures, docs, comments and UI text still use invented names only
context: main's history before the fork is authored by the original author's noreply address; the Windows port commits and their sift entries carry the current maintainer's git identity, and the repo rule says real names stay out of fixtures, docs, comments and UI text
decision: Work since the fork is the maintainer's and is authored under their own git identity, in commits and in sift's who field; the invented-names rule covers the repo's content, not authorship
title: Commits and sift entries since the fork carry the maintainer's own identity

consequences: Sift takes who from git's user.email, so a session recording to sift sets that address for the command (for example GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=user.email GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=<noreply>) or has it as the repo's user.email; any entry with another address is rewritten before a pull request.
context: D-20261015-01 had the Windows port's sift entries carry the maintainer's own git identity, which put a personal email address in a public repo's committed records. The pre-fork entries carry the original author's GitHub noreply address.
decision: Work since the fork is recorded in sift's who field under the maintainer's GitHub noreply address (232592224+angus-pearce@users.noreply.github.com), as the pre-fork entries are under the original author's; the earlier entries were rewritten to it. Git commit authorship is a separate matter and is left as it is. Fixtures, docs, comments and UI text still use invented names only.
title: Sift's who field since the fork is the maintainer's GitHub noreply address

consequences: macOS is unchanged: its window close never quits. A new quit path on Windows chooses whether it asks by its payload.
context: Upstream's Quit dialog ("Quit Brainstead?") answers every quit-requested event. On Windows with no tray icon, closing the window quits through that same event, and the dialog's advice to close the window instead made no sense there.
decision: quit-requested carries the payload "unasked" when the window's close quits (Windows, Show in the menu bar off) and for Brainstead --quit; src/Quit.tsx then asks only about unsaved edits. Explicit quits (the tray's Quit Brainstead, macOS's Cmd+Q and app menu) still ask. The dialog's hint names the menu bar on macOS, the system tray on Windows with the icon shown, and is left out when closing would quit.
title: Quit on Windows: the tray's Quit asks, closing the window and the install script's --quit do not

consequences: The NSIS installer's Restart Manager check still stops every process using the installed exe, MCP servers included, because Windows can't replace a program file in use; assistants reconnect after an install or update on Windows.
context: tools/install_windows.py ran taskkill /IM Brainstead.exe /F, which also killed MCP servers assistants had started (Brainstead.exe --mcp) and any dev build, and gave the app no chance to ask about unsaved edits.
decision: A second launch with --quit from the same program file (checked by canonical path, since every build shares the app identifier's single-instance lock) quits the running copy as a window close does. With no copy running, --quit exits at once. The script finds the installed copy's window process by its executable path, less --mcp command lines, asks it with --quit, waits 10 seconds, then stops only those PIDs.
title: Brainstead --quit asks the installed copy to quit; the install script never kills by image name

consequences: Two copies with the same BRAINSTEAD_DATA can run together; that is a developer's choice. The capture shortcut belongs to whichever copy registered it first.
context: tauri-plugin-single-instance keys its lock on the app identifier, shared by the installed app and every dev build, so on Windows a dev copy handed over to whichever copy was running and exited, though docs/development.md says BRAINSTEAD_DATA separates them.
decision: The plugin is registered only when there is no screenshot scene and BRAINSTEAD_DATA is unset.
title: A copy with BRAINSTEAD_DATA skips the single-instance lock

consequences: Shipping a signed NSIS updater package in latest.json is the follow-up that turns this on.
context: Upstream's updater reads latest.json from GitHub releases, which tools/update_files.py writes for the macOS package only; on Windows every check would fail with no package for the platform, logged hourly.
decision: platform::release_updates() is true on macOS only, and updates::start does nothing elsewhere. README, docs/day-to-day.md and the Settings About help say to install a new version with its installer on Windows.
title: No update checks on Windows until releases carry a Windows package

consequences: A test covers both forms.
context: Upstream's Copy path joins the vault folder and the vault path with a slash, which gives a path with mixed separators on Windows: the vault folder in backslashes, then the vault path in slashes.
decision: fullPath uses a backslash, and turns the vault path's slashes into backslashes, when the root is a drive or UNC path; otherwise it is unchanged.
title: Copy path joins with the vault root's own separator

consequences: Upgrading single-instance is a separate change, tested against the double-launch race.
context: The port forked at 1.0.0 (f25dcf9); upstream reached 1.1.7 (cddcf7c) with 44 commits. A merge and a rebase both conflict in 16 files.
decision: The ten port commits are replayed onto cddcf7c, keeping upstream's behaviour where both sides changed and porting it to Windows. Cargo.lock is upstream's with the port's crates added, and tauri-plugin-single-instance stays at 2.5.2, the version tested on Windows, rather than re-resolving to 2.5.4.
title: The Windows port is rebased onto upstream, with tauri-plugin-single-instance kept at 2.5.2

consequences: Changes record the page as it is on disk, which on macOS and Windows may differ in case from what the assistant typed. A symlinked note whose file is outside the vault can no longer be changed by an assistant, matching the index, which skips links. A Windows path with a colon or a trailing dot or space is refused everywhere a vault-relative path is checked.
context: The hold rules (a change in Templates/ waits for the user, D-20261005-09, D-20261005-11, D-20261005-14) compared path text, and on Windows one file has many names: any case, backslashes, the 8.3 short name, a trailing dot that Win32 drops, an NTFS stream such as Templates::$INDEX_ALLOCATION.
decision: Every page an assistant or run names is read back as the file system spells it (paths::vault_rel: canonical against the vault root, the nearest existing folder for a file not there yet, a rename's new name kept as given) before the rules see it, in the MCP server's page lookup and in the app's submit_many. A path whose real file is outside the vault (a link out) is refused. On Windows is_vault_relative refuses a colon anywhere and a segment ending in a dot or space. The template check also splits on both separators and ignores case as a backstop.
title: Agent changes are ruled on by the file's own path

consequences: Every way to quit on Windows (File > Exit, the tray's Quit, closing the window with the tray off) goes through the window's quit-requested flow. The keyboard help says Ctrl+Q quits only on a Mac and from the menu bar window.
context: tauri's default File menu on Windows ends with the predefined Quit, which muda carries out as PostQuitMessage: the event loop ends with no ExitRequested, so unsaved edits are not asked about, the window state is not saved and assistant runs are not stopped.
decision: On Windows File holds the predefined Close Window and an Exit item of the app's own (id app:exit, label E&xit), which quits through tray::tray_quit as the tray's Quit does. Like the predefined item it replaces, it has no accelerator: the window handles its own keys, and nothing binds Ctrl+Q in the main window on Windows. macOS and Linux keep tauri's default menus.
title: Windows File menu: the app's own Exit

consequences: A new feature flag is added in one place, core/src/features.rs, and reaches the window, the Note menu and app_status from there. A rule that both Rust and TypeScript need still gets side-by-side copies with a fixture test (keyLabel and windows_keys); a rule only Rust needs gets one copy in core.
context: The first Windows port carried PlatformFeatures four times: a struct in the app's platform module, a JSON copy in the MCP crate with a test that the two agreed, and an all-true default table in both src/api.ts and src/features.ts. The 8.3 short-name test helper was copied into the core and MCP test modules, each with its own windows-sys dev-dependency, and the Templates hold rule trimmed trailing dots and spaces that is_vault_relative already refuses.
decision: brainstead_core::features holds the one PlatformFeatures table and its describe() text; the app re-exports it and the MCP server's app_status calls it, so there is nothing to compare. The window keeps one default table, in src/features.ts, and api.platformFeatures is a plain invoke. paths::short_name is a public cfg(windows) helper in core, with windows-sys a cfg(windows) dependency of core alone. in_templates only ignores case and separator; the trailing-dot and space refusals live in is_vault_relative. The npm shim resolver and the Rust glyph rewriter (help::windows_keys, used by the MCP help tool and twelve tool descriptions) stay: each does something the window side cannot.
title: Platform features are one table in core, read by the app and the MCP server

consequences: Changes gains a kind for an added binary file. Help, docs and README describe add_image.
context: Agents could write notes but not the images they embed; only the editor's paste and drop saved images.
decision: An MCP tool add_image takes a file path or base64 bytes plus a name, saves the image to images/ with the paste's naming (never overwriting), and returns its path and embed. The type comes from the bytes; SVG is allowed and applies at once like any other image. It is recorded in Changes as an added image, applied at once even unattended; Revert moves it to Brainstead's Trash. Refused while read-only.
title: Agents add images to the vault with add_image

consequences: The UI mocks artifact is no longer the whole reference for these screens: the mockups for this refresh are. Notes and Templates lose their File column (the path shows on hover over the title). Each step updates help, docs and screenshot scenes in the same change.
context: The screens felt unattractive: every list and side panel was its own bordered box, uppercase tracked labels everywhere, blue on everything, pill-heavy task rows and crowded title bars. Mockups of the proposed look (Today, Inbox, Changes, a note) were made and approved by the user on 2026-10-19.
decision: Restyle in seven steps: (1) no boxes round lists and side panels, sentence-case headings instead of uppercase labels, plain grey counts, file paths on hover; (2) task details as one grey line, only overdue dates coloured; (3) sidebar trimmed, Draft reply, Meeting notes and Compare move to Capture and the palette; (4) title bars keep one or two actions, the rest under a More menu, explanations move to tooltips and help; (5) Today's stat tiles become a summary sentence; (6) Inbox clarify shows the suggestion first and groups the choices as needs doing / doesn't; (7) read-only as one banner with a button to turn it off, and a held change shows one status with its next step. Colour tokens stay; blue is kept for the main action and links. Settings groups, inputs, dialogs and popovers keep their boxes.
title: UX refresh: calmer screens, hierarchy from type and space

consequences: Coming up this week is a new Today list, so it needs a read tool in the MCP server (same names as the screen), help and docs in the same change.
context: On a full-screen window on a large display (about 1800 x 1125) Today left a lot of empty space. A mockup was approved by the user on 2026-10-19.
decision: Part of step 5 of the UX refresh (D-20261019-01). From about 1500 px of content width Today shows a second column beside the task list: Coming up this week (new: tasks due in the next 7 days), Waiting for (with how long, amber after a week) and Deferred, opened rather than folded. The task list stays at most about 620 px wide, and the right rail shows the daily summary's text. Narrower windows fold the second column under the first.
title: Today on a large window: a second column, not wider rows

consequences: ⌘K still lists every screen, Tools' three included, under Go to. The Sidebar tests check the Tools menu and the missing Search row.
context: Step 3 of the UX refresh (D-20261019-01) trims the sidebar. Draft reply, Meeting notes and Compare show progress in the sidebar, and Ask shows unseen answers, so removing them loses that status. The user chose on 2026-10-19.
decision: The three tools sit behind one Tools row at the end of Library, which opens a menu of them; the row carries their spinner and count and is lit while one is open. Ask keeps its row in the daily group. Search loses its row: the search box at the top, ⌥⌘6 and ⌘K reach it (Sidebar's ELSEWHERE list keeps it in ⌘K). Changes moves to the foot with Knowledge health, Activity, Trash and Settings. Counts that want attention are bold dark text, not filled blue badges (amber when a check went wrong).
title: Sidebar: one Tools menu, Ask kept, no Search row

consequences: Text in the accent colour must use accent-ink in dark (the accent is now for fills, icons and borders). The ground is unchanged, so the window's background in Rust is too.
context: After the UX refresh (D-20261019-01) the dark screens looked worse than the light ones: a pale accent with dark text on buttons, heavy navy selections, glowing pastel red and amber, a sidebar darker than the page and greys too close together. The user asked for a dark token pass on 2026-10-19.
decision: Dark accent #2f6fdb with white text (on-accent #fff), accent-soft #1b2535, red #e5776a, amber #d9a24e, green #5bbf8c and their soft fills toned down; side #1b1e23 (lighter than the ground, which stays #16181c), surface #1f2228, lines #2c3038 / #3b4049, ink2 #b3bac5 and ink3 #858d99 further apart. accent-ink stays #8ab8ff for links. The same values in a note's own dark look (.docsurf[data-doc-theme=dark]) and the splash in index.html.
title: Dark tokens retuned to match the light look

consequences: Supersedes D-20261019-03's Search part; the Sidebar test checks the Search row again.
context: D-20261019-03 took Search out of the sidebar (the search box, ⌥⌘6 and ⌘K reach it). The user said on 2026-10-19 that removing it wasn't right.
decision: Search is back as the first row of Library. The rest of D-20261019-03 stands (the Tools menu, Ask kept, Changes at the foot, bold counts).
title: Search keeps its sidebar row

consequences: HOTKEYS must follow the sidebar's order when rows move. Help, docs and tooltips name the new keys.
context: The ⌥⌘ screen keys were a fixed list that fell out of the sidebar's order after the refresh (D-20261019-03, -05), and ⌘1 to ⌘3 were a note's View, Edit and Source. The user chose on 2026-10-19.
decision: ⌘1 to ⌘9 and ⌘0 go to Today, Inbox, Tasks, Projects, Weekly review, Ask, Search, Notes, Wiki and Sources, the sidebar's first ten rows in order (Sidebar's HOTKEYS). A note's View, Edit and Source are ⌥⌘1, ⌥⌘2 and ⌥⌘3, in the Note menu too, matched by the key's place. Changes has no number key.
title: ⌘1 to ⌘0 go to the sidebar's first ten rows

consequences: A new screen with a left pane uses one of the two tokens, not a width of its own.
context: The left panes had six widths (200 to 480 px) and two nav-item styles, which threw off the look. The user asked on 2026-10-19 for Inbox, Tasks, Search, Wiki and Settings to match, and Projects and Changes to match.
decision: Tokens --pane-left (260 px: Inbox, Tasks, Search, Wiki and tags, Settings, Meeting notes, the weekly steps) and --pane-list (400 px: Projects, Changes), narrowed to 220 / 340 px at 1280 px and --pane-left 200 px at 1100 px by the media queries changing the tokens. A pane's nav item (.tnode, Settings' panes) is 30 px tall at 13 px, selected in accent-soft with ink text.
title: Two left-pane widths, one nav-item look

consequences: A new screen needs a guide step that links to it or the help test fails. New guides are guide-*.md files with kind: guide; the order field sets their place in the list.
context: Two-edged Sword offers its Getting started guide at launch and its help has a Getting started button and a topic picker at the top. Brainstead's drawer listed the guides, the screen's keys and every topic as chips below each topic, which pushed the topic down and repeated itself on every screen.
decision: A welcome (src/help/GuideOffer.tsx) offers Getting started once a launch on a vault, until Don't ask me again or Settings › General's switch (settings.offerGuide, on unless false; the MCP settings tool has it) turns it off; never in screenshot mode unless a scene sets guideOffer. Under the drawer's search box: a Getting started button (the guide list, view.start) and an All topics picker (SearchPick). Nothing follows the topic: the guide list, the inline keys and the topic chips are gone. Keyboard shortcuts is a topic like any other and opens on the current screen's keys (KEY_SECTION). The guides cover every screen (help.test.ts checks each screen is an app: link from some guide). MCP open takes help: getting-started, a guide or a topic.
title: Getting started is offered when the app opens; the help drawer's top has Getting started and a topic picker

consequences: A type's colour can change when the commonest types change order; past six, names share a tone. Tag pills stay grey; only the pies colour tags.
context: Graph nodes, the Glance pies and the layer squares used two palettes: notes were purple and sources orange on the Graph but blue and brown as squares, and note types and tags took pie colours by rank, so a tag's colour changed with the counts. Type pills were plain grey.
decision: Layers (note, wiki, source, template) are their --l-* colour wherever they show, the Graph's notes, sources and untyped wiki pages included. Types and tags take one of six tones (--pie-1 to --pie-6, chosen apart from the layer colours; src/tones.ts): the wiki's entity, concept and summary are fixed; the vault's other types, and its tags (notes' and wiki's together), are assigned commonest first, each its letters' tone unless a commoner name has it, so the six commonest never share. src/typeTone.tsx holds the shared glance fetch and the assignment, and TypeDot/TypePill draw a type pill with its dot (Notes, Wiki, Search, the note header, the type filters, Graph's pane). The Graph's Sources and summaries chip is split into Summaries (a wiki type) and Sources (the layer); the MCP graph tool's hide takes the new chip names.
title: One colour per type and tag everywhere; layers keep their own colours, Graph included

consequences: Help, docs and tooltips keep the Mac glyphs and keyLabel words them. A new ⌥⌘letter shortcut stays Ctrl+Alt+letter on Windows; only digits move to Shift. A test in menu.rs and platform.test.ts covers both.
context: The Windows port (PR #1) mapped the screen shortcuts ⌥⌘1 to ⌥⌘0 to Ctrl+Shift+digit. Since it forked, main moved the screens to ⌘1 to ⌘0 and a note's View, Edit and Source to ⌥⌘1 to ⌥⌘3 (D-20261019-06). Ctrl+Alt is AltGr on many layouts.
decision: On Windows ⌘digit is Ctrl+digit (screens) and ⌥⌘digit is Ctrl+Shift+digit (View, Edit, Source): keyLabel already words them so, isOptCmd (was isScreenMod) tests the second, and menu.rs's accel() gives the Note menu's accelerators the same keys off macOS.
title: Windows keys after the merge with main's ⌘1 to ⌘0: screens are Ctrl+digit, a note's View, Edit and Source Ctrl+Shift+1 to 3

consequences: The voice setting on Windows stores a voiceURI. Pausing relies on speechSynthesis.pause, which needs checking on a real Windows machine, as do word boundaries for natural voices. Adding Windows media keys (SMTC) or keep-awake (SetThreadExecutionState) later is a platform-module change only.
context: Read aloud was macOS only (AVSpeechSynthesizer in platform/speech.rs), hidden on Windows by the readAloud feature. WebKit's speechSynthesis was rejected on macOS because it hides Premium and Enhanced voices and pauses unreliably, but WebView2's has Windows' voices, and the sibling app Two-edged Sword already reads aloud that way.
decision: On every platform but macOS, src/speech/player.ts speaks through src/speech/webSpeech.ts (the web view's speechSynthesis), which sends the same word and end events as the macOS module; macOS is unchanged. The readAloud feature is on for Windows (core/src/features.rs), still off on Linux. A paragraph is said in pieces of at most 220 characters at sentence ends, as one utterance with the paragraph's word positions and a single end, because Chromium's speech can stop a long utterance part-way. Natural voices rank as Premium. Now Playing and the media keys, and keeping the screen awake, are skipped on Windows for now: media_state and keep_awake do nothing there.
title: Read aloud on Windows uses WebView2's speechSynthesis; no Now Playing there

consequences: The Windows update reaches a release some minutes after the Mac's; until then Check for Updates... on Windows says the newest release has no update for this system yet. The secrets must be set on the repository before the first release, and windows-cache.yml's bump-commit filter matches 'Brainstead 1.' only. An older release gets its installer by running the workflow by hand with the tag.
context: Windows support (PR #1) shipped a per-user NSIS installer, but releases carried only the Mac package, so Windows copies had no updates (platform::release_updates was macOS only). The sibling apps already publish Windows installers from CI.
decision: Publishing a release (make release, on the Mac) starts .github/workflows/windows-release.yml, which builds the tag on windows-latest and runs tools/update_windows.py: the installer copied to the fixed name Brainstead_x64-setup.exe (the README links to releases/latest/download/ of it), signed with npx tauri signer sign using the TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY(+_PASSWORD) secrets (the same updater key as the Mac's), and windows-x86_64 added to the release's latest.json, re-uploaded with gh release upload --clobber. windows-cache.yml builds main (no bundle) so the release restores its crates (rust-cache shared-key windows-release, save-if false on the tag, same RUSTFLAGS); it skips version-bump-only pushes. Actions on Node 24 versions. release_updates() is on for macOS and Windows; Windows gets Help > Check for Updates... as it has no app menu. The updater's Windows installMode is passive. Release notes get an Installing section (Gatekeeper, SmartScreen: More info, Run anyway).
title: Windows releases and updates: a Windows runner adds the installer to each release

consequences: Choosing Stay at the unsaved-edits question leaves the download unused; the next check offers it again. The --mcp servers are stopped by the installer on Windows, as already documented.
context: On Windows tauri-plugin-updater's install runs the NSIS installer and calls process::exit at once, and the installer closes the app as it starts, so the window could not ask about unsaved edits and RunEvent::ExitRequested's work (window state, stopping assistant runs) never ran. The sibling apps run before_quit in the download-finished callback, which still skips the unsaved-edits question.
decision: On Windows Install and Restart only downloads (Update::download) and keeps the bytes; restart_for_update then asks the window as on macOS, and app_restart calls updates::install_downloaded, which runs crate::before_quit (shared with ExitRequested) and then Update::install. If the installer fails to start the user is told and the app keeps running. Leftover %TEMP%\Brainstead-*-updater-* folders are deleted at startup (platform::remove_update_installers). The uninstall hook removes %APPDATA%\Brainstead (core paths::data_dir, not the bundle id) and those folders only with Delete the application data ticked and never for an update ($UpdateMode <> 1); the vault is never touched.
title: Windows update: download on Install, install from app_restart after the quit work

consequences: A save can take up to a second longer on Windows before failing; macOS behaviour is unchanged. The retry loop is tested by injecting errors, so it runs on every platform; the Windows error classification is only checked on Windows CI.
context: On Windows a rename over a file another process has open (antivirus, OneDrive sync, an editor, the MCP server reading bridge/alive.json) fails briefly with access denied or a sharing or lock violation; dev builds popped a console; drag regions on Windows act as title bar, so the elements stop scrolling and taking clicks. Two-edged Sword and Tidemark hit the same.
decision: Every rename (write_atomic, the bridge's files, settings, Changes' migration, the Trash, note renames) goes through core write::rename: up to ten tries over about a second, doubling from 10 ms, only on Windows errors 5, 32 and 33; other errors and other systems fail at once. Bridge readers try a failed open twice more, and a claimed request that can't be read is put back. main.rs is windows_subsystem in every Windows build. data-tauri-drag-region is spread from dragRegion() (macOS only) and the traffic-light room is kept for macOS only.
title: Windows: renames retry while a file is held open; no console in any build; drag regions macOS only

consequences: A new Note or Help menu item with a key the window doesn't already handle needs a WINDOW_KEYS line, or it has no key on Windows; the test only checks the lines that are there. Quitting on Windows is the tray's Quit Brainstead (or closing the window with the tray off).
context: PR #1 kept tauri's default menus on Windows (File with its own Exit, Edit, Window, Help) plus the Note menu (D-20261015-03). Two-edged Sword and Tidemark have no menu bar on Windows. Everything in the Note menu is in a note's ⋯ menu and Ctrl+K, and the tray quits as Exit did; but some note keys (Ctrl+P, Ctrl+Shift+P, Ctrl+Alt+C, Ctrl+Alt+R, Ctrl+Shift+R, Ctrl+., Ctrl+Shift+/) came only from the menu's accelerators.
decision: Supersedes D-20261015-03. menu::install puts up no menu bar on Windows (macOS and Linux keep theirs); the Windows File menu and its Exit are gone. src/noteMenu.ts WINDOW_KEYS lists the menu-only keys as menu.rs has them (a test reads menu.rs) and, on Windows, emits the same menu event the item would. Check for Updates… is a button in Settings › About on Windows, and the MCP server's check_updates does the same everywhere.
title: No menu bar on Windows; the window takes the menu's keys and About has Check for Updates

consequences: The footer's look is kept in two places, PDFKit's stamp (macOS) and pdfFooter (Windows). An old WebView2 without ICoreWebView2_7 gets an error asking to update it.
context: Export PDF was Mac only: WKWebView's print, then PDFKit stamps the title and Page N of M footer and drops the blank page WebKit adds after a forced break. Neither sibling app exports PDFs.
decision: On Windows platform::print_to_pdf calls ICoreWebView2_7::PrintToPdf with the user's locale paper (A4, or Letter where LOCALE_IPAPERSIZE says so), 0.5in margins, no browser header or footer and no backgrounds. The footer is print style (src/notes/actions.ts pdfFooter: @page margin boxes with counter(page) and counter(pages)), so no PDF library is needed; Chromium repeats table headers, so tables aren't split and no blank page is dropped. exportPdf is on for Windows in core::features.
title: Export PDF on Windows: WebView2's PrintToPdf, the footer from print style

consequences: Harper adds a few MB and a long first compile on Windows only. Words added go to Windows' user dictionary, shared with other apps, as on macOS.
context: The editor's spelling and grammar marks were Mac only (NSSpellChecker). Windows gives apps a spell checker (ISpellChecker, Edge's and Office's) but no grammar checker; Two-edged Sword's journal uses Harper for grammar there.
decision: platform/spell_win.rs is the Windows twin of spell.rs, with the same functions: spelling by ISpellChecker, one per language per thread, languages named as on macOS (en_GB) and given to Windows as en-GB; grammar by harper-core's curated checks in the dialect of the chosen English, limited to the kinds that are grammar (not spelling or style), a lone lowercase i reported as macOS does, and a problem that is the whole sentence (a fragment) or inside another left out. Harper is made off the main thread at start (platform::spell_warm). spelling and grammar are on for Windows in core::features.
title: Spelling and grammar on Windows as Two-edged Sword's journal: Windows' spell checker and Harper

consequences: A PC with no text recognition language gets an error saying where to add one. HEIC and WebP read only where their Microsoft Store extensions are installed. Text recognition's quality is Windows', not Vision's.
context: Reading the text in images (Vision) and the JPEG a model is shown (sips) were Mac only, so on Windows an image's text wasn't indexed or ingested and images couldn't be shown to an assistant.
decision: platform/image_win.rs reads the file through Windows.Graphics.Imaging (BitmapDecoder from the file's bytes) for both: Windows.Media.Ocr in the user's profile languages, the image scaled to the engine's largest size, for image_text; and a JPEG with its longest side at most 2000 px, turned upright and in sRGB, for image_for_model. image_text is on for Windows in core::features.
title: The text in images and images for a model on Windows: Windows' own imaging and text recognition

consequences: Retake them with python3 tools/screenshots.py --fresh --theme light and the tut* scene names. A change to a screen the tutorials show, or to an MCP tool name used in power.html, should update the tutorial in the same change. New scene options: docMenu, crop, chat: tutorial, replyDraft, and data.
context: The website needed step-by-step tutorials for non-technical users, in the product page's style.
decision: site/tutorials/ holds an index and four pages (beginner, intermediate, advanced, power) that follow one invented story (organising Acme's office move) across the levels. Each has a Mac / Windows PC switch at the top that swaps every key (data-win), install steps and words such as menu bar, remembered per browser. Their pictures are tut* scenes in tools/screenshots/scenes.json, taken from demo vaults written by tools/screenshots/demo_tutorial.py (data: tutorial, intermediate, advanced, power, welcome), never from the fixture vault. The power tutorial shows terminal sessions with Brainstead's real MCP tool names; other services' steps are described in words, except Atlassian's tool names.
title: Website tutorials: four levels, one office-move story, pictures from screenshot scenes

consequences: Keep the cards two a row at 400px (the .levels width); a new card needs its own crop scene and both files.
context: The tutorial cards' pictures were whole screenshots scaled down to about 340px, so their text blurred on 1x monitors (fine on Retina).
decision: Each card's scene crops 400 by 250 at the app's own scale; the card is 400px wide and draws it at that size, framed as a small app window on a tinted panel under the card's text. tools/screenshots.py saves a <name>-light@1x.webp beside the 2x picture when that file exists, and the page uses srcset.
title: Tutorial card pictures are cropped at the size they're shown, with a 1x copy

consequences: Crops in scenes.json stay at the docs' 1400 width; the tool scales them. Keep the cards two a row at 400px.
context: D-20261021-02 cut the cards' 1x pictures from the 1400-wide docs copy, about 3% under the 1440-point window's own size, so they weren't quite 1:1.
decision: The 1x copy is cut from the snapshot at the window's own width in points (411 by 257 for a 400 by 250 crop given at the docs' 1400 width) and the 2x copy at twice that; the card draws the picture at its own size (width: auto) in a 400px card that crops what doesn't fit, framed as a small app window under the card's text.
title: Tutorial card pictures are cut at the window's own size in points

consequences: Sync stops if Teams isn't opened in Chrome for about a day; Settings shows the token state. The endpoints are undocumented or deprecated (Outlook REST v2.0) and can change without notice, so every call fails soft and is reported in Settings rather than breaking capture. The user's tokens leave Chrome, but only to the local app and the Keychain. The extensions stay the manual way to capture.
context: The user wants chats, meeting transcripts, inbox mail and calendar to reach Sources without clicking capture. Microsoft Graph is ruled out. A spike (2026-10-25, Mac) showed: Teams and Outlook on the web keep MSAL tokens in localStorage, including a refresh token (SPA, about 24 hours); those tokens work outside the browser against chatsvc (chats, meeting chats), Outlook REST v2.0 (full mail bodies, calendar view with attendees and bodies) and the Teams middle-tier calendar. A separate sign-in window (WKWebView) worked once but asked for the password again on every launch on a managed work account, so it can't run unattended.
decision: No separate sign-in. While Teams (and optionally Outlook) is open in Chrome, the Teams and Outlook capture extensions read the page's token cache and hand it to Brainstead over the existing native-messaging host.
